units.leftText: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
units.rightText: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.

units.leftText: He was with God in the beginning.
units.rightText: The same was in the beginning with God.

units.leftText: Through Him all things were made, and without Him nothing was made that has been made.
units.rightText: All things were made through him; and without him was not anything made that hath been made.

units.leftText: In Him was life, and that life was the light of men.
units.rightText: In him was life; and the life was the light of men.

units.leftText: The Light shines in the darkness, and the darkness has not overcome it. The Witness of John
units.rightText: And the light shineth in the darkness; and the darkness apprehended it not.
leftNotes: 1:5 Or comprehended

units.leftText: There came a man who was sent from God. His name was John.
units.rightText: There came a man, sent from God, whose name was John.

units.leftText: He came as a witness to testify about the Light, so that through him everyone might believe.
units.rightText: The same came for witness, that he might bear witness of the light, that all might believe through him.

units.leftText: He himself was not the Light, but he came to testify about the Light.
units.rightText: He was not the light, but came that he might bear witness of the light.

units.leftText: The true Light, who gives light to everyone, was coming into the world.
units.rightText: There was the true light, even the light which lighteth every man, coming into the world.

units.leftText: He was in the world, and though the world was made through Him, the world did not recognize Him.
units.rightText: He was in the world, and the world was made through him, and the world knew him not.

units.leftText: He came to His own, and His own did not receive Him.
units.rightText: He came unto his own, and they that were his own received him not.

units.leftText: But to all who did receive Him, to those who believed in His name, He gave the right to become children of God —
units.rightText: But as many as received him, to them gave he the right to become children of God, even to them that believe on his name:

units.leftText: children born not of blood, nor of the desire or will of man, but born of God. The Word Became Flesh (Psalm 84:1–12|PSA 84:1-12*)
units.rightText: who were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God.

units.leftText: The Word became flesh and made His dwelling among us. We have seen His glory, the glory of the one and only Son from the Father, full of grace and truth.
units.rightText: And the Word became flesh, and dwelt among us (and we beheld his glory, glory as of the only begotten from the Father), full of grace and truth.
leftNotes: 1:14 Or and tabernacled among us
1:14 Or the Only Begotten or the Unique One

units.leftText: John testified concerning Him. He cried out, saying, “This is He of whom I said, ‘He who comes after me has surpassed me because He was before me.’”
units.rightText: John beareth witness of him, and crieth, saying, This was he of whom I said, He that cometh after me is become before me: for he was before me.

units.leftText: From His fullness we have all received grace upon grace.
units.rightText: For of his fulness we all received, and grace for grace.

units.leftText: For the law was given through Moses; grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.
units.rightText: For the law was given through Moses; grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.

units.leftText: No one has ever seen God, but the one and only Son, who is Himself God and is at the Father’s side, has made Him known. The Mission of John the Baptist (Isaiah 40:1–5|ISA 40:1-5*; Matthew 3:1–12|MAT 3:1-12*; Mark 1:1–8|MRK 1:1-8*; Luke 3:1–20|LUK 3:1-20*)
units.rightText: No man hath seen God at any time; the only begotten Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, he hath declared him.
leftNotes: 1:18 Or but the only begotten God, who; BYZ and TR but the only begotten Son, who
1:18 Greek in the Father’s bosom

units.leftText: And this was John’s testimony when the Jews of Jerusalem sent priests and Levites to ask him, “Who are you?”
units.rightText: And this is the witness of John, when the Jews sent unto him from Jerusalem priests and Levites to ask him, Who art thou?

units.leftText: He did not refuse to confess, but openly declared, “I am not the Christ.”
units.rightText: And he confessed, and denied not; and he confessed, I am not the Christ.

units.leftText: “Then who are you?” they inquired. “Are you Elijah?” He said, “I am not.” “Are you the Prophet?” He answered, “No.”
units.rightText: And they asked him, What then? Art thou Elijah? And he saith, I am not. Art thou the prophet? And he answered, No.

units.leftText: So they said to him, “Who are you? We need an answer for those who sent us. What do you say about yourself?”
units.rightText: They said therefore unto him, Who art thou? that we may give an answer to them that sent us. What sayest thou of thyself?

units.leftText: John replied in the words of Isaiah the prophet: “I am a voice of one calling in the wilderness, ‘Make straight the way for the Lord.’”
units.rightText: He said, I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness, Make straight the way of the Lord, as said Isaiah the prophet.
leftNotes: 1:23 Isaiah 40:3|ISA 40:3* (see also LXX)

units.leftText: Then the Pharisees who had been sent
units.rightText: And they had been sent from the Pharisees.

units.leftText: asked him, “Why then do you baptize, if you are not the Christ, nor Elijah, nor the Prophet?”
units.rightText: And they asked him, and said unto him, Why then baptizest thou, if thou art not the Christ, neither Elijah, neither the prophet?

units.leftText: “I baptize with water,” John replied, “but among you stands One you do not know.
units.rightText: John answered them, saying, I baptize in water: in the midst of you standeth one whom ye know not,
leftNotes: 1:26 Or in; also in verse 31 and twice in 33

units.leftText: He is the One who comes after me, the straps of whose sandals I am not worthy to untie.”
units.rightText: even he that cometh after me, the latchet of whose shoe I am not worthy to unloose.

units.leftText: All this happened at Bethany beyond the Jordan, where John was baptizing. Jesus the Lamb of God (Matthew 3:13–17|MAT 3:13-17*; Mark 1:9–11|MRK 1:9-11*; Luke 3:21–22|LUK 3:21-22*)
units.rightText: These things were done in Bethany beyond the Jordan, where John was baptizing.

units.leftText: The next day John saw Jesus coming toward him and said, “Look, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!
units.rightText: On the morrow he seeth Jesus coming unto him, and saith, Behold, the Lamb of God, that taketh away the sin of the world!

units.leftText: This is He of whom I said, ‘A man who comes after me has surpassed me because He was before me.’
units.rightText: This is he of whom I said, After me cometh a man who is become before me: for he was before me.

units.leftText: I myself did not know Him, but the reason I came baptizing with water was that He might be revealed to Israel.”
units.rightText: And I knew him not; but that he should be made manifest to Israel, for this cause came I baptizing in water.

units.leftText: Then John testified, “I saw the Spirit descending from heaven like a dove and resting on Him.
units.rightText: And John bare witness, saying, I have beheld the Spirit descending as a dove out of heaven; and it abode upon him.

units.leftText: I myself did not know Him, but the One who sent me to baptize with water told me, ‘The man on whom you see the Spirit descend and rest is He who will baptize with the Holy Spirit.’
units.rightText: And I knew him not: but he that sent me to baptize in water, he said unto me, Upon whomsoever thou shalt see the Spirit descending, and abiding upon him, the same is he that baptizeth in the Holy Spirit.

units.leftText: I have seen and testified that this is the Son of God. ” The First Disciples (Matthew 4:18–22|MAT 4:18-22*; Mark 1:16–20|MRK 1:16-20*; Luke 5:1–11|LUK 5:1-11*)
units.rightText: And I have seen, and have borne witness that this is the Son of God.
leftNotes: 1:34 SBL the Chosen One of God

units.leftText: The next day John was there again with two of his disciples.
units.rightText: Again on the morrow John was standing, and two of his disciples;

units.leftText: When he saw Jesus walking by, he said, “Look, the Lamb of God!”
units.rightText: and he looked upon Jesus as he walked, and saith, Behold, the Lamb of God!

units.leftText: And when the two disciples heard him say this, they followed Jesus.
units.rightText: And the two disciples heard him speak, and they followed Jesus.

units.leftText: Jesus turned and saw them following. “What do you want?” He asked. They said to Him, “Rabbi” (which means Teacher), “where are You staying?”
units.rightText: And Jesus turned, and beheld them following, and saith unto them, What seek ye? And they said unto him, Rabbi (which is to say, being interpreted, Teacher), where abidest thou?

units.leftText: “Come and see,” He replied. So they went and saw where He was staying, and spent that day with Him. It was about the tenth hour.
units.rightText: He saith unto them, Come, and ye shall see. They came therefore and saw where he abode; and they abode with him that day: it was about the tenth hour.
leftNotes: 1:39 That is, about four in the afternoon

units.leftText: Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother, was one of the two who heard John’s testimony and followed Jesus.
units.rightText: One of the two that heard John speak, and followed him, was Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother.

units.leftText: He first found his brother Simon and told him, “We have found the Messiah” (which is translated as Christ).
units.rightText: He findeth first his own brother Simon, and saith unto him, We have found the Messiah (which is, being interpreted, Christ).

units.leftText: Andrew brought him to Jesus, who looked at him and said, “You are Simon son of John. You will be called Cephas” (which is translated as Peter). Jesus Calls Philip and Nathanael
units.rightText: He brought him unto Jesus. Jesus looked upon him, and said, Thou art Simon the son of John: thou shalt be called Cephas (which is by interpretation, Peter).

units.leftText: The next day Jesus decided to set out for Galilee. Finding Philip, He told him, “Follow Me.”
units.rightText: On the morrow he was minded to go forth into Galilee, and he findeth Philip: and Jesus saith unto him, Follow me.

units.leftText: Now Philip was from Bethsaida, the same town as Andrew and Peter.
units.rightText: Now Philip was from Bethsaida, of the city of Andrew and Peter.

units.leftText: Philip found Nathanael and told him, “We have found the One Moses wrote about in the Law, the One the prophets foretold — Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph.”
units.rightText: Philip findeth Nathanael, and saith unto him, We have found him, of whom Moses in the law, and the prophets, wrote, Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph.

units.leftText: “Can anything good come from Nazareth?” Nathanael asked. “Come and see,” said Philip.
units.rightText: And Nathanael said unto him, Can any good thing come out of Nazareth? Philip saith unto him, Come and see.

units.leftText: When Jesus saw Nathanael approaching, He said of him, “Here is a true Israelite, in whom there is no deceit.”
units.rightText: Jesus saw Nathanael coming to him, and saith of him, Behold, an Israelite indeed, in whom is no guile!

units.leftText: “How do You know me?” Nathanael asked. Jesus replied, “Before Philip called you, I saw you under the fig tree.”
units.rightText: Nathanael saith unto him, Whence knowest thou me? Jesus answered and said unto him, Before Philip called thee, when thou wast under the fig tree, I saw thee.

units.leftText: “Rabbi,” Nathanael answered, “You are the Son of God! You are the King of Israel!”
units.rightText: Nathanael answered him, Rabbi, thou art the Son of God; thou art King of Israel.

units.leftText: Jesus said to him, “Do you believe just because I told you I saw you under the fig tree? You will see greater things than these.”
units.rightText: Jesus answered and said unto him, Because I said unto thee, I saw thee underneath the fig tree, believest thou? thou shalt see greater things than these.

units.leftText: Then He declared, “Truly, truly, I tell you, you will all see heaven open and the angels of God ascending and descending on the Son of Man.”
units.rightText: And he saith unto him, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Ye shall see the heaven opened, and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of man.
leftNotes: 1:51 See Genesis 28:12|GEN 28:12*.

units.leftText: On the third day a wedding took place at Cana in Galilee. Jesus’ mother was there,
units.rightText: And the third day there was a marriage in Cana of Galilee; and the mother of Jesus was there:

units.leftText: and Jesus and His disciples had also been invited to the wedding.
units.rightText: and Jesus also was bidden, and his disciples, to the marriage.

units.leftText: When the wine ran out, Jesus’ mother said to Him, “They have no more wine.”
units.rightText: And when the wine failed, the mother of Jesus saith unto him, They have no wine.

units.leftText: “Woman, what is that to you and to Me?” Jesus replied. “My hour has not yet come.”
units.rightText: And Jesus saith unto her, Woman, what have I to do with thee? mine hour is not yet come.

units.leftText: His mother said to the servants, “Do whatever He tells you.”
units.rightText: His mother saith unto the servants, Whatsoever he saith unto you, do it.

units.leftText: Now six stone water jars had been set there for the Jewish rites of purification. Each could hold from twenty to thirty gallons.
units.rightText: Now there were six waterpots of stone set there after the Jews’ manner of purifying, containing two or three firkins apiece.
leftNotes: 2:6 Greek two or three metretae; that is, approximately 20.8 to 31.2 gallons (78.8 to 118.1 liters)

units.leftText: Jesus told the servants, “Fill the jars with water.” So they filled them to the brim.
units.rightText: Jesus saith unto them, Fill the waterpots with water. And they filled them up to the brim.

units.leftText: “Now draw some out,” He said, “and take it to the master of the banquet.”
units.rightText: And he saith unto them, Draw out now, and bear unto the ruler of the feast. And they bare it.

units.leftText: and the master of the banquet tasted the water that had been turned into wine. He did not know where it was from, but the servants who had drawn the water knew. Then he called the bridegroom aside
units.rightText: And when the ruler of the feast tasted the water now become wine, and knew not whence it was (but the servants that had drawn the water knew), the ruler of the feast calleth the bridegroom,

units.leftText: and said, “Everyone serves the fine wine first, and then the cheap wine after the guests are drunk. But you have saved the fine wine until now!”
units.rightText: and saith unto him, Every man setteth on first the good wine; and when men have drunk freely, then that which is worse: thou hast kept the good wine until now.

units.leftText: Jesus performed this, the first of His signs, at Cana in Galilee. He thus revealed His glory, and His disciples believed in Him. Jesus Cleanses the Temple (Matthew 21:12–17|MAT 21:12-17*; Mark 11:15–19|MRK 11:15-19*; Luke 19:45–48|LUK 19:45-48*)
units.rightText: This beginning of his signs did Jesus in Cana of Galilee, and manifested his glory; and his disciples believed on him.

units.leftText: After this, He went down to Capernaum with His mother and brothers and His disciples, and they stayed there a few days.
units.rightText: After this he went down to Capernaum, he, and his mother, and his brethren, and his disciples; and there they abode not many days.

units.leftText: When the Jewish Passover was near, Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
units.rightText: And the passover of the Jews was at hand, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.

units.leftText: In the temple courts He found men selling cattle, sheep, and doves, and money changers seated at their tables.
units.rightText: And he found in the temple those that sold oxen and sheep and doves, and the changers of money sitting:
leftNotes: 2:14 Literally the temple; also in verse 15

units.leftText: So He made a whip out of cords and drove all from the temple courts, both sheep and cattle. He poured out the coins of the money changers and overturned their tables.
units.rightText: and he made a scourge of cords, and cast all out of the temple, both the sheep and the oxen; and he poured out the changers’ money, and overthrew their tables;

units.leftText: To those selling doves He said, “Get these out of here! How dare you turn My Father’s house into a marketplace!”
units.rightText: and to them that sold the doves he said, Take these things hence; make not my Father’s house a house of merchandise.

units.leftText: His disciples remembered that it is written: “Zeal for Your house will consume Me.”
units.rightText: His disciples remembered that it was written, Zeal for thy house shall eat me up.

units.leftText: On account of this, the Jews demanded, “What sign can You show us to prove Your authority to do these things?”
units.rightText: The Jews therefore answered and said unto him, What sign showest thou unto us, seeing that thou doest these things?

units.leftText: Jesus answered, “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up again.”
units.rightText: Jesus answered and said unto them, Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.

units.leftText: “This temple took forty-six years to build,” the Jews replied, “and You are going to raise it up in three days?”
units.rightText: The Jews therefore said, Forty and six years was this temple in building, and wilt thou raise it up in three days?

units.leftText: But Jesus was speaking about the temple of His body.
units.rightText: But he spake of the temple of his body.

units.leftText: After He was raised from the dead, His disciples remembered that He had said this. Then they believed the Scripture and the word that Jesus had spoken.
units.rightText: When therefore he was raised from the dead, his disciples remembered that he spake this; and they believed the scripture, and the word which Jesus had said.

units.leftText: While He was in Jerusalem at the Passover Feast, many people saw the signs He was doing and believed in His name.
units.rightText: Now when he was in Jerusalem at the passover, during the feast, many believed on his name, beholding his signs which he did.

units.leftText: But Jesus did not entrust Himself to them, for He knew them all.
units.rightText: But Jesus did not trust himself unto them, for that he knew all men,

units.leftText: He did not need any testimony about man, for He knew what was in a man.
units.rightText: and because he needed not that any one should bear witness concerning man; for he himself knew what was in man.

units.leftText: Now there was a man of the Pharisees named Nicodemus, a leader of the Jews.
units.rightText: Now there was a man of the Pharisees, named Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews:

units.leftText: He came to Jesus at night and said, “Rabbi, we know that You are a teacher who has come from God. For no one could perform the signs You are doing if God were not with him.”
units.rightText: the same came unto him by night, and said to him, Rabbi, we know that thou art a teacher come from God; for no one can do these signs that thou doest, except God be with him.

units.leftText: Jesus replied, “Truly, truly, I tell you, no one can see the kingdom of God unless he is born again. ”
units.rightText: Jesus answered and said unto him, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except one be born anew, he cannot see the kingdom of God.
leftNotes: 3:3 Or born from above; also in verse 7.

units.leftText: “How can a man be born when he is old?” Nicodemus asked. “Can he enter his mother’s womb a second time to be born?”
units.rightText: Nicodemus saith unto him, How can a man be born when he is old? can he enter a second time into his mother’s womb, and be born?

units.leftText: Jesus answered, “Truly, truly, I tell you, no one can enter the kingdom of God unless he is born of water and the Spirit.
units.rightText: Jesus answered, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except one be born of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God.

units.leftText: Flesh is born of flesh, but spirit is born of the Spirit.
units.rightText: That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit.

units.leftText: Do not be amazed that I said, ‘You must be born again.’
units.rightText: Marvel not that I said unto thee, Ye must be born anew.
leftNotes: 3:7 The Greek word for you is plural; also in verse 12.

units.leftText: The wind blows where it wishes. You hear its sound, but you do not know where it comes from or where it is going. So it is with everyone born of the Spirit.”
units.rightText: The wind bloweth where it will, and thou hearest the voice thereof, but knowest not whence it cometh, and whither it goeth: so is every one that is born of the Spirit.

units.leftText: “How can this be?” Nicodemus asked.
units.rightText: Nicodemus answered and said unto him, How can these things be?

units.leftText: “You are Israel’s teacher,” said Jesus, “and you do not understand these things?
units.rightText: Jesus answered and said unto him, Art thou the teacher of Israel, and understandest not these things?

units.leftText: Truly, truly, I tell you, we speak of what we know, and we testify to what we have seen, and yet you people do not accept our testimony.
units.rightText: Verily, verily, I say unto thee, We speak that which we know, and bear witness of that which we have seen; and ye receive not our witness.

units.leftText: If I have told you about earthly things and you do not believe, how will you believe if I tell you about heavenly things?
units.rightText: If I told you earthly things and ye believe not, how shall ye believe if I tell you heavenly things?

units.leftText: No one has ascended into heaven except the One who descended from heaven— the Son of Man.
units.rightText: And no one hath ascended into heaven, but he that descended out of heaven, even the Son of man, who is in heaven.
leftNotes: 3:13 BYZ and TR include who is in heaven.

units.leftText: Just as Moses lifted up the snake in the wilderness, so the Son of Man must be lifted up,
units.rightText: And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up;

units.leftText: that everyone who believes in Him may have eternal life.
units.rightText: that whosoever believeth may in him have eternal life.
leftNotes: 3:15 Or everyone who believes may have eternal life in Him.

units.leftText: For God so loved the world that He gave His one and only Son, that everyone who believes in Him shall not perish but have eternal life.
units.rightText: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth on him should not perish, but have eternal life.
leftNotes: 3:16 Or only begotten or unique; also in verse 18

units.leftText: For God did not send His Son into the world to condemn the world, but to save the world through Him.
units.rightText: For God sent not the Son into the world to judge the world; but that the world should be saved through him.

units.leftText: Whoever believes in Him is not condemned, but whoever does not believe has already been condemned, because he has not believed in the name of God’s one and only Son.
units.rightText: He that believeth on him is not judged: he that believeth not hath been judged already, because he hath not believed on the name of the only begotten Son of God.

units.leftText: And this is the verdict: The Light has come into the world, but men loved the darkness rather than the Light because their deeds were evil.
units.rightText: And this is the judgment, that the light is come into the world, and men loved the darkness rather than the light; for their works were evil.

units.leftText: Everyone who does evil hates the Light, and does not come into the Light for fear that his deeds will be exposed.
units.rightText: For every one that doeth evil hateth the light, and cometh not to the light, lest his works should be reproved.

units.leftText: But whoever practices the truth comes into the Light, so that it may be seen clearly that what he has done has been accomplished in God.” John’s Testimony about Jesus
units.rightText: But he that doeth the truth cometh to the light, that his works may be made manifest, that they have been wrought in God.
leftNotes: 3:21 Some translators close this quotation after verse 15.

units.leftText: After this, Jesus and His disciples went into the Judean countryside, where He spent some time with them and baptized.
units.rightText: After these things came Jesus and his disciples into the land of Judæa; and there he tarried with them, and baptized.

units.leftText: Now John was also baptizing at Aenon near Salim, because the water was plentiful there, and people kept coming to be baptized.
units.rightText: And John also was baptizing in Ænon near to Salim, because there was much water there: and they came, and were baptized.

units.leftText: (For John had not yet been thrown into prison.)
units.rightText: For John was not yet cast into prison.

units.leftText: Then a dispute arose between John’s disciples and a certain Jew over the issue of ceremonial washing.
units.rightText: There arose therefore a questioning on the part of John’s disciples with a Jew about purifying.
leftNotes: 3:25 TR and the Jews

units.leftText: So John’s disciples came to him and said, “Look, Rabbi, the One who was with you beyond the Jordan, the One you testified about — He is baptizing, and everyone is going to Him.”
units.rightText: And they came unto John, and said to him, Rabbi, he that was with thee beyond the Jordan, to whom thou hast borne witness, behold, the same baptizeth, and all men come to him.

units.leftText: John replied, “A man can receive only what is given him from heaven.
units.rightText: John answered and said, A man can receive nothing, except it have been given him from heaven.

units.leftText: You yourselves can testify that I said, ‘I am not the Christ, but am sent ahead of Him.’
units.rightText: Ye yourselves bear me witness, that I said, I am not the Christ, but, that I am sent before him.

units.leftText: The bride belongs to the bridegroom. The friend of the bridegroom stands and listens for him, and is overjoyed to hear the bridegroom’s voice. That joy is mine, and it is now complete.
units.rightText: He that hath the bride is the bridegroom: but the friend of the bridegroom, that standeth and heareth him, rejoiceth greatly because of the bridegroom’s voice: this my joy therefore is made full.

units.leftText: He must increase; I must decrease.
units.rightText: He must increase, but I must decrease.

units.leftText: The One who comes from above is above all. The one who is from the earth belongs to the earth and speaks as one from the earth. The One who comes from heaven is above all.
units.rightText: He that cometh from above is above all: he that is of the earth is of the earth, and of the earth he speaketh: he that cometh from heaven is above all.
leftNotes: 3:31 Tischendorf The One comes from heaven.

units.leftText: He testifies to what He has seen and heard, yet no one accepts His testimony.
units.rightText: What he hath seen and heard, of that he beareth witness; and no man receiveth his witness.

units.leftText: Whoever accepts His testimony has certified that God is truthful.
units.rightText: He that hath received his witness hath set his seal to this, that God is true.

units.leftText: For the One whom God has sent speaks the words of God, for God gives the Spirit without limit.
units.rightText: For he whom God hath sent speaketh the words of God: for he giveth not the Spirit by measure.

units.leftText: The Father loves the Son and has placed all things in His hands.
units.rightText: The Father loveth the Son, and hath given all things into his hand.

units.leftText: Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life. Whoever rejects the Son will not see life. Instead, the wrath of God remains on him.”
units.rightText: He that believeth on the Son hath eternal life; but he that obeyeth not the Son shall not see life, but the wrath of God abideth on him.
leftNotes: 3:36 Some translators close this quotation after verse 30.

units.leftText: When Jesus realized that the Pharisees were aware He was gaining and baptizing more disciples than John
units.rightText: When therefore the Lord knew that the Pharisees had heard that Jesus was making and baptizing more disciples than John
leftNotes: 4:1 Literally When therefore Jesus knew that the Pharisees had heard that Jesus; NE, WH, BYZ, and TR When therefore the Lord knew that the Pharisees had heard that Jesus

units.leftText: (although it was not Jesus who baptized, but His disciples),
units.rightText: (although Jesus himself baptized not, but his disciples),

units.leftText: He left Judea and returned to Galilee.
units.rightText: he left Judæa, and departed again into Galilee.

units.leftText: Now He had to pass through Samaria.
units.rightText: And he must needs pass through Samaria.

units.leftText: So He came to a town of Samaria called Sychar, near the plot of ground that Jacob had given to his son Joseph.
units.rightText: So he cometh to a city of Samaria, called Sychar, near to the parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph:

units.leftText: Since Jacob’s well was there, Jesus, weary from His journey, sat down by the well. It was about the sixth hour.
units.rightText: and Jacob’s well was there. Jesus therefore, being wearied with his journey, sat thus by the well. It was about the sixth hour.
leftNotes: 4:6 That is, about noon

units.leftText: When a Samaritan woman came to draw water, Jesus said to her, “Give Me a drink.”
units.rightText: There cometh a woman of Samaria to draw water: Jesus saith unto her, Give me to drink.

units.leftText: (His disciples had gone into the town to buy food.)
units.rightText: For his disciples were gone away into the city to buy food.

units.leftText: “You are a Jew,” said the woman. “How can You ask for a drink from me, a Samaritan woman?” (For Jews do not associate with Samaritans.)
units.rightText: The Samaritan woman therefore saith unto him, How is it that thou, being a Jew, askest drink of me, who am a Samaritan woman? (For Jews have no dealings with Samaritans.)
leftNotes: 4:9 Tischendorf does not include this sentence.

units.leftText: Jesus answered, “If you knew the gift of God and who is asking you for a drink, you would have asked Him, and He would have given you living water.”
units.rightText: Jesus answered and said unto her, If thou knewest the gift of God, and who it is that saith to thee, Give me to drink; thou wouldest have asked of him, and he would have given thee living water.

units.leftText: “Sir,” the woman replied, “You have nothing to draw with and the well is deep. Where then will You get this living water?
units.rightText: The woman saith unto him, Sir, thou hast nothing to draw with, and the well is deep: whence then hast thou that living water?

units.leftText: Are You greater than our father Jacob, who gave us this well and drank from it himself, as did his sons and his livestock?”
units.rightText: Art thou greater than our father Jacob, who gave us the well, and drank thereof himself, and his sons, and his cattle?

units.leftText: Jesus said to her, “Everyone who drinks this water will be thirsty again.
units.rightText: Jesus answered and said unto her, Every one that drinketh of this water shall thirst again:

units.leftText: But whoever drinks the water I give him will never thirst. Indeed, the water I give him will become in him a fount of water springing up to eternal life.”
units.rightText: but whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; but the water that I shall give him shall become in him a well of water springing up unto eternal life.

units.leftText: The woman said to Him, “Sir, give me this water so that I will not get thirsty and have to keep coming here to draw water.”
units.rightText: The woman saith unto him, Sir, give me this water, that I thirst not, neither come all the way hither to draw.

units.leftText: Jesus told her, “Go, call your husband and come back.”
units.rightText: Jesus saith unto her, Go, call thy husband, and come hither.

units.leftText: “I have no husband,” the woman replied.
units.rightText: The woman answered and said unto him, I have no husband. Jesus saith unto her, Thou saidst well, I have no husband:

units.leftText: In fact, you have had five husbands, and the man you now have is not your husband. You have spoken truthfully.”
units.rightText: for thou hast had five husbands; and he whom thou now hast is not thy husband: this hast thou said truly.

units.leftText: “Sir,” the woman said, “I see that You are a prophet.
units.rightText: The woman saith unto him, Sir, I perceive that thou art a prophet.

units.leftText: Our fathers worshiped on this mountain, but you Jews say that the place where one must worship is in Jerusalem.”
units.rightText: Our fathers worshipped in this mountain; and ye say, that in Jerusalem is the place where men ought to worship.

units.leftText: “Believe Me, woman,” Jesus replied, “a time is coming when you will worship the Father neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem.
units.rightText: Jesus saith unto her, Woman, believe me, the hour cometh, when neither in this mountain, nor in Jerusalem, shall ye worship the Father.

units.leftText: You worship what you do not know; we worship what we do know, for salvation is from the Jews.
units.rightText: Ye worship that which ye know not: we worship that which we know; for salvation is from the Jews.

units.leftText: But a time is coming and has now come when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and in truth, for the Father is seeking such as these to worship Him.
units.rightText: But the hour cometh, and now is, when the true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit and truth: for such doth the Father seek to be his worshippers.

units.leftText: God is Spirit, and His worshipers must worship Him in spirit and in truth.”
units.rightText: God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship in spirit and truth.

units.leftText: The woman said, “I know that Messiah” (called Christ) “is coming. When He comes, He will explain everything to us.”
units.rightText: The woman saith unto him, I know that Messiah cometh (he that is called Christ): when he is come, he will declare unto us all things.

units.leftText: Jesus answered, “I who speak to you am He.” The Disciples Return and Marvel
units.rightText: Jesus saith unto her, I that speak unto thee am he.

units.leftText: Just then His disciples returned and were surprised that He was speaking with a woman. But no one asked Him, “What do You want from her?” or “Why are You talking with her?”
units.rightText: And upon this came his disciples; and they marvelled that he was speaking with a woman; yet no man said, What seekest thou? or, Why speakest thou with her?

units.leftText: Then the woman left her water jar, went back into the town, and said to the people,
units.rightText: So the woman left her waterpot, and went away into the city, and saith to the people,

units.leftText: “Come, see a man who told me everything I ever did. Could this be the Christ?”
units.rightText: Come, see a man, who told me all things that ever I did: can this be the Christ?

units.leftText: So they left the town and made their way toward Jesus.
units.rightText: They went out of the city, and were coming to him.

units.leftText: Meanwhile the disciples urged Him, “Rabbi, eat something.”
units.rightText: In the mean while the disciples prayed him, saying, Rabbi, eat.

units.leftText: But He told them, “I have food to eat that you know nothing about.”
units.rightText: But he said unto them, I have meat to eat that ye know not.

units.leftText: So the disciples asked one another, “Could someone have brought Him food?”
units.rightText: The disciples therefore said one to another, Hath any man brought him aught to eat?

units.leftText: Jesus explained, “My food is to do the will of Him who sent Me and to finish His work.
units.rightText: Jesus saith unto them, My meat is to do the will of him that sent me, and to accomplish his work.

units.leftText: Do you not say, ‘There are still four months until the harvest’? I tell you, lift up your eyes and look at the fields, for they are ripe for harvest.
units.rightText: Say not ye, There are yet four months, and then cometh the harvest? behold, I say unto you, Lift up your eyes, and look on the fields, that they are white already unto harvest.
leftNotes: 4:35 Literally white

units.leftText: Already the reaper draws his wages and gathers a crop for eternal life, so that the sower and the reaper may rejoice together.
units.rightText: He that reapeth receiveth wages, and gathereth fruit unto life eternal; that he that soweth and he that reapeth may rejoice together.

units.leftText: For in this case the saying ‘One sows and another reaps’ is true.
units.rightText: For herein is the saying true, One soweth, and another reapeth.

units.leftText: I sent you to reap what you have not worked for; others have done the hard work, and now you have taken up their labor.” Many Samaritans Believe
units.rightText: I sent you to reap that whereon ye have not labored: others have labored, and ye are entered into their labor.

units.leftText: Many of the Samaritans from that town believed in Jesus because of the woman’s testimony, “He told me everything I ever did.”
units.rightText: And from that city many of the Samaritans believed on him because of the word of the woman, who testified, He told me all things that ever I did.

units.leftText: So when the Samaritans came to Him, they asked Him to stay with them, and He stayed two days.
units.rightText: So when the Samaritans came unto him, they besought him to abide with them: and he abode there two days.

units.leftText: And many more believed because of His message.
units.rightText: And many more believed because of his word;

units.leftText: They said to the woman, “We now believe not only because of your words; we have heard for ourselves, and we know that this man truly is the Savior of the world.” Jesus Heals the Official’s Son (Matthew 8:5–13|MAT 8:5-13*; Luke 7:1–10|LUK 7:1-10*)
units.rightText: and they said to the woman, Now we believe, not because of thy speaking: for we have heard for ourselves, and know that this is indeed the Saviour of the world.

units.leftText: After two days, Jesus left for Galilee.
units.rightText: And after the two days he went forth from thence into Galilee.

units.leftText: Now He Himself had testified that a prophet has no honor in his own hometown.
units.rightText: For Jesus himself testified, that a prophet hath no honor in his own country.

units.leftText: Yet when He arrived, the Galileans welcomed Him. They had seen all the great things He had done in Jerusalem at the feast, for they had gone there as well.
units.rightText: So when he came into Galilee, the Galilæans received him, having seen all the things that he did in Jerusalem at the feast: for they also went unto the feast.

units.leftText: So once again He came to Cana in Galilee, where He had turned the water into wine. And there was a royal official whose son lay sick at Capernaum.
units.rightText: He came therefore again unto Cana of Galilee, where he made the water wine. And there was a certain nobleman, whose son was sick at Capernaum.

units.leftText: When he heard that Jesus had come from Judea to Galilee, he went and begged Him to come down and heal his son, who was about to die.
units.rightText: When he heard that Jesus was come out of Judæa into Galilee, he went unto him, and besought him that he would come down, and heal his son; for he was at the point of death.

units.leftText: Jesus said to him, “Unless you people see signs and wonders, you will never believe.”
units.rightText: Jesus therefore said unto him, Except ye see signs and wonders, ye will in no wise believe.

units.leftText: “Sir,” the official said, “come down before my child dies.”
units.rightText: The nobleman saith unto him, Sir, come down ere my child die.

units.leftText: “Go,” said Jesus. “Your son will live.”
units.rightText: Jesus saith unto him, Go thy way; thy son liveth. The man believed the word that Jesus spake unto him, and he went his way.

units.leftText: And while he was still on the way, his servants met him with the news that his boy was alive.
units.rightText: And as he was now going down, his servants met him, saying, that his son lived.

units.leftText: So he inquired as to the hour when his son had recovered, and they told him, “The fever left him yesterday at the seventh hour. ”
units.rightText: So he inquired of them the hour when he began to amend. They said therefore unto him, Yesterday at the seventh hour the fever left him.
leftNotes: 4:52 That is, one in the afternoon

units.leftText: Then the father realized that this was the very hour in which Jesus had told him, “Your son will live.” And he and all his household believed.
units.rightText: So the father knew that it was at that hour in which Jesus said unto him, Thy son liveth: and himself believed, and his whole house.

units.leftText: This was now the second sign that Jesus performed after coming from Judea into Galilee.
units.rightText: This is again the second sign that Jesus did, having come out of Judæa into Galilee.

units.leftText: Some time later there was a feast of the Jews, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
units.rightText: After these things there was a feast of the Jews; and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.

units.leftText: Now there is in Jerusalem near the Sheep Gate a pool with five covered colonnades, which in Hebrew is called Bethesda.
units.rightText: Now there is in Jerusalem by the sheep gate a pool, which is called in Hebrew Bethesda, having five porches.
leftNotes: 5:2 Or in Aramaic
5:2 NA, NE, and WH Bethzatha

units.leftText: On these walkways lay a great number of the sick, the blind, the lame, and the paralyzed.
units.rightText: In these lay a multitude of them that were sick, blind, halt, withered.
leftNotes: 5:3 Literally In these

5:3 NE, BYZ, and TR include awaiting the moving of the waters. 4*For from time to time an angel descended into the pool and stirred the water. As soon as it was stirred, the first to enter the pool would be healed of his disease.

rightNotes: 5:4 Many ancient authorities insert, wholly or in part, waiting for the moving of the water: for an angel of the Lord went down at certain seasons into the pool, and troubled the water: whosoever then first after the troubling of the water stepped in was made whole, with whatsoever disease he was holden.

units.leftText: One man there had been an invalid for thirty-eight years.
units.rightText: And a certain man was there, who had been thirty and eight years in his infirmity.

units.leftText: When Jesus saw him lying there and realized that he had spent a long time in this condition, He asked him, “Do you want to get well?”
units.rightText: When Jesus saw him lying, and knew that he had been now a long time in that case, he saith unto him, Wouldest thou be made whole?

units.leftText: “Sir,” the invalid replied, “I have no one to help me into the pool when the water is stirred. While I am on my way, someone else goes in before me.”
units.rightText: The sick man answered him, Sir, I have no man, when the water is troubled, to put me into the pool: but while I am coming, another steppeth down before me.

units.leftText: Then Jesus told him, “Get up, pick up your mat, and walk.”
units.rightText: Jesus saith unto him, Arise, take up thy bed, and walk.

units.leftText: Immediately the man was made well, and he picked up his mat and began to walk.
units.rightText: And straightway the man was made whole, and took up his bed and walked. Now it was the sabbath on that day.

units.leftText: so the Jews said to the man who had been healed, “This is the Sabbath! It is unlawful for you to carry your mat.”
units.rightText: So the Jews said unto him that was cured, It is the sabbath, and it is not lawful for thee to take up thy bed.

units.leftText: But he answered, “The man who made me well told me, ‘Pick up your mat and walk.’”
units.rightText: But he answered them, He that made me whole, the same said unto me, Take up thy bed, and walk.

units.leftText: “Who is this man who told you to pick it up and walk?” they asked.
units.rightText: They asked him, Who is the man that said unto thee, Take up thy bed, and walk?

units.leftText: But the man who was healed did not know who it was, for Jesus had slipped away while the crowd was there.
units.rightText: But he that was healed knew not who it was; for Jesus had conveyed himself away, a multitude being in the place.

units.leftText: Afterward, Jesus found the man at the temple and said to him, “See, you have been made well. Stop sinning, or something worse may happen to you.”
units.rightText: Afterward Jesus findeth him in the temple, and said unto him, Behold, thou art made whole: sin no more, lest a worse thing befall thee.

units.leftText: And the man went away and told the Jews that it was Jesus who had made him well. The Father and the Son
units.rightText: The man went away, and told the Jews that it was Jesus who had made him whole.

units.leftText: Now because Jesus was doing these things on the Sabbath, the Jews began to persecute Him.
units.rightText: And for this cause the Jews persecuted Jesus, because he did these things on the sabbath.

units.leftText: But Jesus answered them, “To this very day My Father is at His work, and I too am working.”
units.rightText: But Jesus answered them, My Father worketh even until now, and I work.

units.leftText: Because of this, the Jews tried all the harder to kill Him. Not only was He breaking the Sabbath, but He was even calling God His own Father, making Himself equal with God.
units.rightText: For this cause therefore the Jews sought the more to kill him, because he not only brake the sabbath, but also called God his own Father, making himself equal with God.

units.leftText: So Jesus replied, “Truly, truly, I tell you, the Son can do nothing by Himself, unless He sees the Father doing it. For whatever the Father does, the Son also does.
units.rightText: Jesus therefore answered and said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, The Son can do nothing of himself, but what he seeth the Father doing: for what things soever he doeth, these the Son also doeth in like manner.

units.leftText: The Father loves the Son and shows Him all He does. And to your amazement, He will show Him even greater works than these.
units.rightText: For the Father loveth the Son, and showeth him all things that himself doeth: and greater works than these will he show him, that ye may marvel.

units.leftText: For just as the Father raises the dead and gives them life, so also the Son gives life to whom He wishes.
units.rightText: For as the Father raiseth the dead and giveth them life, even so the Son also giveth life to whom he will.

units.leftText: Furthermore, the Father judges no one, but has assigned all judgment to the Son,
units.rightText: For neither doth the Father judge any man, but he hath given all judgment unto the Son;

units.leftText: so that all may honor the Son just as they honor the Father. Whoever does not honor the Son does not honor the Father who sent Him.
units.rightText: that all may honor the Son, even as they honor the Father. He that honoreth not the Son honoreth not the Father that sent him.

units.leftText: Truly, truly, I tell you, whoever hears My word and believes Him who sent Me has eternal life and will not come under judgment. Indeed, he has crossed over from death to life.
units.rightText: Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that heareth my word, and believeth him that sent me, hath eternal life, and cometh not into judgment, but hath passed out of death into life.

units.leftText: Truly, truly, I tell you, the hour is coming and has now come when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear will live.
units.rightText: Verily, verily, I say unto you, The hour cometh, and now is, when the dead shall hear the voice of the Son of God; and they that hear shall live.

units.leftText: For as the Father has life in Himself, so also He has granted the Son to have life in Himself.
units.rightText: For as the Father hath life in himself, even so gave he to the Son also to have life in himself:

units.leftText: And He has given Him authority to execute judgment, because He is the Son of Man.
units.rightText: and he gave him authority to execute judgment, because he is a son of man.

units.leftText: Do not be amazed at this, for the hour is coming when all who are in their graves will hear His voice
units.rightText: Marvel not at this: for the hour cometh, in which all that are in the tombs shall hear his voice,

units.leftText: and come out — those who have done good to the resurrection of life, and those who have done evil to the resurrection of judgment.
units.rightText: and shall come forth; they that have done good, unto the resurrection of life; and they that have done evil, unto the resurrection of judgment.
leftNotes: 5:29 See Daniel 12:2|DAN 12:2*.

units.leftText: I can do nothing by Myself; I judge only as I hear. And My judgment is just, because I do not seek My own will, but the will of Him who sent Me. Testimonies about Jesus
units.rightText: I can of myself do nothing: as I hear, I judge: and my judgment is righteous; because I seek not mine own will, but the will of him that sent me.

units.leftText: If I testify about Myself, My testimony is not valid.
units.rightText: If I bear witness of myself, my witness is not true.

units.leftText: There is another who testifies about Me, and I know that His testimony about Me is valid.
units.rightText: It is another that beareth witness of me; and I know that the witness which he witnesseth of me is true.

units.leftText: You have sent to John, and he has testified to the truth.
units.rightText: Ye have sent unto John, and he hath borne witness unto the truth.

units.leftText: Even though I do not accept human testimony, I say these things so that you may be saved.
units.rightText: But the witness which I receive is not from man: howbeit I say these things, that ye may be saved.

units.leftText: John was a lamp that burned and gave light, and you were willing for a season to bask in his light.
units.rightText: He was the lamp that burneth and shineth; and ye were willing to rejoice for a season in his light.

units.leftText: But I have testimony more substantial than that of John. For the works that the Father has given Me to accomplish — the very works I am doing — testify about Me that the Father has sent Me.
units.rightText: But the witness which I have is greater than that of John; for the works which the Father hath given me to accomplish, the very works that I do, bear witness of me, that the Father hath sent me.

units.leftText: And the Father who sent Me has Himself testified about Me. You have never heard His voice nor seen His form,
units.rightText: And the Father that sent me, he hath borne witness of me. Ye have neither heard his voice at any time, nor seen his form.

units.leftText: nor does His word abide in you, because you do not believe the One He sent. The Witness of Scripture (Luke 16:19–31|LUK 16:19-31*)
units.rightText: And ye have not his word abiding in you: for whom he sent, him ye believe not.

units.leftText: You pore over the Scriptures because you presume that by them you possess eternal life. These are the very words that testify about Me,
units.rightText: Ye search the scriptures, because ye think that in them ye have eternal life; and these are they which bear witness of me;

units.leftText: yet you refuse to come to Me to have life.
units.rightText: and ye will not come to me, that ye may have life.

units.leftText: I do not accept glory from men,
units.rightText: I receive not glory from men.

units.leftText: but I know you, that you do not have the love of God within you.
units.rightText: But I know you, that ye have not the love of God in yourselves.

units.leftText: I have come in My Father’s name, and you have not received Me; but if someone else comes in his own name, you will receive him.
units.rightText: I am come in my Father’s name, and ye receive me not: if another shall come in his own name, him ye will receive.

units.leftText: How can you believe if you accept glory from one another, yet do not seek the glory that comes from the only God?
units.rightText: How can ye believe, who receive glory one of another, and the glory that cometh from the only God ye seek not?

units.leftText: Do not think that I will accuse you before the Father. Your accuser is Moses, in whom you have put your hope.
units.rightText: Think not that I will accuse you to the Father: there is one that accuseth you, even Moses, on whom ye have set your hope.

units.leftText: If you had believed Moses, you would believe Me, because he wrote about Me.
units.rightText: For if ye believed Moses, ye would believe me; for he wrote of me.

units.leftText: But since you do not believe what he wrote, how will you believe what I say?”
units.rightText: But if ye believe not his writings, how shall ye believe my words?

units.leftText: After this, Jesus crossed to the other side of the Sea of Galilee ( that is, the Sea of Tiberias ).
units.rightText: After these things Jesus went away to the other side of the sea of Galilee, which is the sea of Tiberias.

units.leftText: A large crowd followed Him because they saw the signs He was performing on the sick.
units.rightText: And a great multitude followed him, because they beheld the signs which he did on them that were sick.

units.leftText: Then Jesus went up on the mountain and sat down with His disciples.
units.rightText: And Jesus went up into the mountain, and there he sat with his disciples.

units.leftText: Now the Jewish Feast of the Passover was near.
units.rightText: Now the passover, the feast of the Jews, was at hand.

units.leftText: When Jesus looked up and saw a large crowd coming toward Him, He said to Philip, “Where can we buy bread for these people to eat?”
units.rightText: Jesus therefore lifting up his eyes, and seeing that a great multitude cometh unto him, saith unto Philip, Whence are we to buy bread, that these may eat?

units.leftText: But He was asking this to test him, for He knew what He was about to do.
units.rightText: And this he said to prove him: for he himself knew what he would do.

units.leftText: Philip answered, “Two hundred denarii would not buy enough bread for each of them to have a small piece.”
units.rightText: Philip answered him, Two hundred shillings’ worth of bread is not sufficient for them, that every one may take a little.
leftNotes: 6:7 A denarius was customarily a day’s wage for a laborer; see Matthew 20:2|MAT 20:2*.

units.leftText: One of His disciples, Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother, said to Him,
units.rightText: One of his disciples, Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother, saith unto him,

units.leftText: “Here is a boy with five barley loaves and two small fish. But what difference will these make among so many?”
units.rightText: There is a lad here, who hath five barley loaves, and two fishes: but what are these among so many?

units.leftText: “Have the people sit down,” Jesus said. Now there was plenty of grass in that place, so the men sat down, about five thousand of them.
units.rightText: Jesus said, Make the people sit down. Now there was much grass in the place. So the men sat down, in number about five thousand.

units.leftText: Then Jesus took the loaves and the fish, gave thanks, and distributed to those who were seated as much as they wanted.
units.rightText: Jesus therefore took the loaves; and having given thanks, he distributed to them that were set down; likewise also of the fishes as much as they would.

units.leftText: And when everyone was full, He said to His disciples, “Gather the pieces that are left over, so that nothing will be wasted.”
units.rightText: And when they were filled, he saith unto his disciples, Gather up the broken pieces which remain over, that nothing be lost.

units.leftText: So they collected them and filled twelve baskets with the pieces of the five barley loaves left over by those who had eaten.
units.rightText: So they gathered them up, and filled twelve baskets with broken pieces from the five barley loaves, which remained over unto them that had eaten.

units.leftText: When the people saw the sign that Jesus had performed, they began to say, “Truly this is the Prophet who is to come into the world.”
units.rightText: When therefore the people saw the sign which he did, they said, This is of a truth the prophet that cometh into the world.
leftNotes: 6:14 SBL, NA, NE, and WH He had performed

units.leftText: Then Jesus, realizing that they were about to come and make Him king by force, withdrew again to a mountain by Himself. Jesus Walks on Water (Matthew 14:22–33|MAT 14:22-33*; Mark 6:45–52|MRK 6:45-52*)
units.rightText: Jesus therefore perceiving that they were about to come and take him by force, to make him king, withdrew again into the mountain himself alone.

units.leftText: When evening came, His disciples went down to the sea,
units.rightText: And when evening came, his disciples went down unto the sea;

units.leftText: got into a boat, and started across the sea to Capernaum. It was already dark, and Jesus had not yet gone out to them.
units.rightText: and they entered into a boat, and were going over the sea unto Capernaum. And it was now dark, and Jesus had not yet come to them.

units.leftText: A strong wind was blowing, and the sea grew agitated.
units.rightText: And the sea was rising by reason of a great wind that blew.

units.leftText: When they had rowed about three or four miles, they saw Jesus approaching the boat, walking on the sea — and they were terrified.
units.rightText: When therefore they had rowed about five and twenty or thirty furlongs, they behold Jesus walking on the sea, and drawing nigh unto the boat: and they were afraid.
leftNotes: 6:19 Greek about twenty-five or thirty stadia; that is, approximately 2.87 to 3.45 miles (4.62 to 5.55 kilometers)

units.leftText: But Jesus spoke up: “It is I; do not be afraid.”
units.rightText: But he saith unto them, It is I; be not afraid.

units.leftText: Then they were willing to take Him into the boat, and at once the boat reached the shore where they were heading. Jesus the Bread of Life
units.rightText: They were willing therefore to receive him into the boat: and straightway the boat was at the land whither they were going.

units.leftText: The next day, the crowd that had remained on the other side of the sea realized that only one boat had been there, and that Jesus had not boarded it with His disciples, but they had gone away alone.
units.rightText: On the morrow the multitude that stood on the other side of the sea saw that there was no other boat there, save one, and that Jesus entered not with his disciples into the boat, but that his disciples went away alone

units.leftText: However, some boats from Tiberias landed near the place where the people had eaten the bread after the Lord had given thanks.
units.rightText: (howbeit there came boats from Tiberias nigh unto the place where they ate the bread after the Lord had given thanks):

units.leftText: So when the crowd saw that neither Jesus nor His disciples were there, they got into the boats and went to Capernaum to look for Him.
units.rightText: when the multitude therefore saw that Jesus was not there, neither his disciples, they themselves got into the boats, and came to Capernaum, seeking Jesus.

units.leftText: When they found Him on the other side of the sea, they asked Him, “Rabbi, when did You get here?”
units.rightText: And when they found him on the other side of the sea, they said unto him, Rabbi, when camest thou hither?

units.leftText: Jesus replied, “Truly, truly, I tell you, it is not because you saw these signs that you are looking for Me, but because you ate the loaves and had your fill.
units.rightText: Jesus answered them and said, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Ye seek me, not because ye saw signs, but because ye ate of the loaves, and were filled.

units.leftText: Do not work for food that perishes, but for food that endures to eternal life, which the Son of Man will give you. For on Him God the Father has placed His seal of approval.”
units.rightText: Work not for the food which perisheth, but for the food which abideth unto eternal life, which the Son of man shall give unto you: for him the Father, even God, hath sealed.

units.leftText: Then they inquired, “What must we do to perform the works of God?”
units.rightText: They said therefore unto him, What must we do, that we may work the works of God?

units.leftText: Jesus replied, “The work of God is this: to believe in the One He has sent.”
units.rightText: Jesus answered and said unto them, This is the work of God, that ye believe on him whom he hath sent.

units.leftText: So they asked Him, “What sign then will You perform, so that we may see it and believe You? What will You do?
units.rightText: They said therefore unto him, What then doest thou for a sign, that we may see, and believe thee? what workest thou?

units.leftText: Our fathers ate the manna in the wilderness, as it is written: ‘He gave them bread from heaven to eat.’ ”
units.rightText: Our fathers ate the manna in the wilderness; as it is written, He gave them bread out of heaven to eat.
leftNotes: 6:31 Psalm 78:24|PSA 78:24*; see also Exodus 16:4.

units.leftText: Jesus said to them, “Truly, truly, I tell you, it was not Moses who gave you the bread from heaven, but it is My Father who gives you the true bread from heaven.
units.rightText: Jesus therefore said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, It was not Moses that gave you the bread out of heaven; but my Father giveth you the true bread out of heaven.

units.leftText: For the bread of God is He who comes down from heaven and gives life to the world.”
units.rightText: For the bread of God is that which cometh down out of heaven, and giveth life unto the world.

units.leftText: “Sir,” they said, “give us this bread at all times.”
units.rightText: They said therefore unto him, Lord, evermore give us this bread.

units.leftText: Jesus answered, “I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to Me will never hunger, and whoever believes in Me will never thirst.
units.rightText: Jesus said unto them, I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall not hunger, and he that believeth on me shall never thirst.

units.leftText: But as I stated, you have seen Me and still you do not believe.
units.rightText: But I said unto you, that ye have seen me, and yet believe not.

units.leftText: Everyone the Father gives Me will come to Me, and the one who comes to Me I will never drive away.
units.rightText: All that which the Father giveth me shall come unto me; and him that cometh to me I will in no wise cast out.

units.leftText: For I have come down from heaven, not to do My own will, but to do the will of Him who sent Me.
units.rightText: For I am come down from heaven, not to do mine own will, but the will of him that sent me.

units.leftText: And this is the will of Him who sent Me, that I shall lose none of those He has given Me, but raise them up at the last day.
units.rightText: And this is the will of him that sent me, that of all that which he hath given me I should lose nothing, but should raise it up at the last day.

units.leftText: For it is My Father’s will that everyone who looks to the Son and believes in Him shall have eternal life, and I will raise him up at the last day.”
units.rightText: For this is the will of my Father, that every one that beholdeth the Son, and believeth on him, should have eternal life; and I will raise him up at the last day.

units.leftText: At this, the Jews began to grumble about Jesus because He had said, “I am the bread that came down from heaven.”
units.rightText: The Jews therefore murmured concerning him, because he said, I am the bread which came down out of heaven.

units.leftText: They were asking, “Is this not Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? How then can He say, ‘I have come down from heaven’?”
units.rightText: And they said, Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? how doth he now say, I am come down out of heaven?

units.leftText: “Stop grumbling among yourselves,” Jesus replied.
units.rightText: Jesus answered and said unto them, Murmur not among yourselves.

units.leftText: “No one can come to Me unless the Father who sent Me draws him, and I will raise him up at the last day.
units.rightText: No man can come to me, except the Father that sent me draw him: and I will raise him up in the last day.

units.leftText: It is written in the Prophets: ‘And they will all be taught by God.’ Everyone who has heard the Father and learned from Him comes to Me —
units.rightText: It is written in the prophets, And they shall all be taught of God. Every one that hath heard from the Father, and hath learned, cometh unto me.

units.leftText: not that anyone has seen the Father except the One who is from God; only He has seen the Father.
units.rightText: Not that any man hath seen the Father, save he that is from God, he hath seen the Father.

units.leftText: Truly, truly, I tell you, he who believes has eternal life.
units.rightText: Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that believeth hath eternal life.

units.leftText: I am the bread of life.
units.rightText: I am the bread of life.

units.leftText: Your fathers ate the manna in the wilderness, yet they died.
units.rightText: Your fathers ate the manna in the wilderness, and they died.

units.leftText: This is the bread that comes down from heaven, so that anyone may eat of it and not die.
units.rightText: This is the bread which cometh down out of heaven, that a man may eat thereof, and not die.

units.leftText: I am the living bread that came down from heaven. If anyone eats of this bread, he will live forever. And this bread, which I will give for the life of the world, is My flesh.”
units.rightText: I am the living bread which came down out of heaven: if any man eat of this bread, he shall live for ever: yea and the bread which I will give is my flesh, for the life of the world.

units.leftText: At this, the Jews began to argue among themselves, “How can this man give us His flesh to eat?”
units.rightText: The Jews therefore strove one with another, saying, How can this man give us his flesh to eat?

units.leftText: So Jesus said to them, “Truly, truly, I tell you, unless you eat the flesh and drink the blood of the Son of Man, you have no life in you.
units.rightText: Jesus therefore said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Except ye eat the flesh of the Son of man and drink his blood, ye have not life in yourselves.

units.leftText: Whoever eats My flesh and drinks My blood has eternal life, and I will raise him up at the last day.
units.rightText: He that eateth my flesh and drinketh my blood hath eternal life; and I will raise him up at the last day.

units.leftText: For My flesh is real food, and My blood is real drink.
units.rightText: For my flesh is meat indeed, and my blood is drink indeed.

units.leftText: Whoever eats My flesh and drinks My blood remains in Me, and I in him.
units.rightText: He that eateth my flesh and drinketh my blood abideth in me, and I in him.

units.leftText: Just as the living Father sent Me and I live because of the Father, so also the one who feeds on Me will live because of Me.
units.rightText: As the living Father sent me, and I live because of the Father; so he that eateth me, he also shall live because of me.

units.leftText: This is the bread that came down from heaven. Unlike your fathers, who ate the manna and died, the one who eats this bread will live forever.” Many Disciples Turn Back (Matthew 8:18–22|MAT 8:18-22*; Luke 9:57–62|LUK 9:57-62*; Luke 14:25–33|LUK 14:25-33*)
units.rightText: This is the bread which came down out of heaven: not as the fathers ate, and died; he that eateth this bread shall live for ever.

units.leftText: Jesus said this while teaching in the synagogue in Capernaum.
units.rightText: These things said he in the synagogue, as he taught in Capernaum.

units.leftText: On hearing it, many of His disciples said, “This is a difficult teaching. Who can accept it?”
units.rightText: Many therefore of his disciples, when they heard this, said, This is a hard saying; who can hear it?

units.leftText: Aware that His disciples were grumbling about this teaching, Jesus asked them, “Does this offend you?
units.rightText: But Jesus knowing in himself that his disciples murmured at this, said unto them, Doth this cause you to stumble?

units.leftText: Then what will happen if you see the Son of Man ascend to where He was before?
units.rightText: What then if ye should behold the Son of man ascending where he was before?

units.leftText: The Spirit gives life; the flesh profits nothing. The words I have spoken to you are spirit and they are life.
units.rightText: It is the spirit that giveth life; the flesh profiteth nothing: the words that I have spoken unto you are spirit, and are life.

units.leftText: However, there are some of you who do not believe.” (For Jesus had known from the beginning which of them did not believe and who would betray Him.)
units.rightText: But there are some of you that believe not. For Jesus knew from the beginning who they were that believed not, and who it was that should betray him.

units.leftText: Then Jesus said, “This is why I told you that no one can come to Me unless the Father has granted it to him.”
units.rightText: And he said, For this cause have I said unto you, that no man can come unto me, except it be given unto him of the Father.

units.leftText: From that time on many of His disciples turned back and no longer walked with Him. Peter’s Confession of Faith (Matthew 16:13–20|MAT 16:13-20*; Mark 8:27–30|MRK 8:27-30*; Luke 9:18–20|LUK 9:18-20*)
units.rightText: Upon this many of his disciples went back, and walked no more with him.

units.leftText: So Jesus asked the Twelve, “Do you want to leave too?”
units.rightText: Jesus said therefore unto the twelve, Would ye also go away?

units.leftText: Simon Peter replied, “Lord, to whom would we go? You have the words of eternal life.
units.rightText: Simon Peter answered him, Lord, to whom shall we go? thou hast the words of eternal life.

units.leftText: We believe and know that You are the Holy One of God. ”
units.rightText: And we have believed and know that thou art the Holy One of God.
leftNotes: 6:69 BYZ and TR You are the Christ, the Son of the living God

units.leftText: Jesus answered them, “Have I not chosen you, the Twelve? Yet one of you is a devil!”
units.rightText: Jesus answered them, Did not I choose you the twelve, and one of you is a devil?

units.leftText: He was speaking about Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot. For although Judas was one of the Twelve, he was later to betray Jesus.
units.rightText: Now he spake of Judas the son of Simon Iscariot, for he it was that should betray him, being one of the twelve.

units.leftText: After this, Jesus traveled throughout Galilee. He did not want to travel in Judea, because the Jews there were trying to kill Him.
units.rightText: And after these things Jesus walked in Galilee: for he would not walk in Judæa, because the Jews sought to kill him.

units.leftText: However, the Jewish Feast of Tabernacles was near.
units.rightText: Now the feast of the Jews, the feast of tabernacles, was at hand.
leftNotes: 7:2 That is, Sukkot, the autumn feast of pilgrimage to Jerusalem; also translated as the Feast of Booths or the Feast of Shelters and originally called the Feast of Ingathering(see Exodus 23:16|EXO 23:16* and Exodus 34:22).

units.leftText: So Jesus’ brothers said to Him, “Leave here and go to Judea, so that Your disciples there may see the works You are doing.
units.rightText: His brethren therefore said unto him, Depart hence, and go into Judæa, that thy disciples also may behold thy works which thou doest.

units.leftText: For no one who wants to be known publicly acts in secret. Since You are doing these things, show Yourself to the world.”
units.rightText: For no man doeth anything in secret, and himself seeketh to be known openly. If thou doest these things, manifest thyself to the world.

units.leftText: For even His own brothers did not believe in Him.
units.rightText: For even his brethren did not believe on him.

units.leftText: Therefore Jesus told them, “Although your time is always at hand, My time has not yet come.
units.rightText: Jesus therefore saith unto them, My time is not yet come; but your time is always ready.

units.leftText: The world cannot hate you, but it hates Me, because I testify that its works are evil.
units.rightText: The world cannot hate you; but me it hateth, because I testify of it, that its works are evil.

units.leftText: Go up to the feast on your own. I am not going up to this feast, because My time has not yet come.”
units.rightText: Go ye up unto the feast: I go not up unto this feast; because my time is not yet fulfilled.
leftNotes: 7:8 NE, WH, BYZ, and TR I am not yet

units.leftText: Having said this, Jesus remained in Galilee.
units.rightText: And having said these things unto them, he abode still in Galilee.

units.leftText: But after His brothers had gone up to the feast, He also went — not publicly, but in secret.
units.rightText: But when his brethren were gone up unto the feast, then went he also up, not publicly, but as it were in secret.

units.leftText: So the Jews were looking for Him at the feast and asking, “Where is He?”
units.rightText: The Jews therefore sought him at the feast, and said, Where is he?

units.leftText: Many in the crowds were whispering about Him. Some said, “He is a good man.” But others replied, “No, He deceives the people.”
units.rightText: And there was much murmuring among the multitudes concerning him: some said, He is a good man; others said, Not so, but he leadeth the multitude astray.

units.leftText: Yet no one would speak publicly about Him for fear of the Jews.
units.rightText: Yet no man spake openly of him for fear of the Jews.

units.leftText: About halfway through the feast, Jesus went up to the temple courts and began to teach.
units.rightText: But when it was now the midst of the feast Jesus went up into the temple, and taught.
leftNotes: 7:14 Literally the temple; also in verse 28

units.leftText: The Jews were amazed and asked, “How did this man attain such learning without having studied?”
units.rightText: The Jews therefore marvelled, saying, How knoweth this man letters, having never learned?

units.leftText: “My teaching is not My own,” Jesus replied. “It comes from Him who sent Me.
units.rightText: Jesus therefore answered them, and said, My teaching is not mine, but his that sent me.

units.leftText: If anyone desires to do His will, he will know whether My teaching is from God or whether I speak on My own.
units.rightText: If any man willeth to do his will, he shall know of the teaching, whether it is of God, or whether I speak from myself.

units.leftText: He who speaks on his own authority seeks his own glory, but He who seeks the glory of the One who sent Him is a man of truth; in Him there is no falsehood.
units.rightText: He that speaketh from himself seeketh his own glory: but he that seeketh the glory of him that sent him, the same is true, and no unrighteousness is in him.

units.leftText: Has not Moses given you the law? Yet not one of you keeps it. Why are you trying to kill Me?”
units.rightText: Did not Moses give you the law, and yet none of you doeth the law? Why seek ye to kill me?

units.leftText: “You have a demon,” the crowd replied. “Who is trying to kill You?”
units.rightText: The multitude answered, Thou hast a demon: who seeketh to kill thee?

units.leftText: Jesus answered them, “I did one miracle, and you are all amazed.
units.rightText: Jesus answered and said unto them, I did one work, and ye all marvel because thereof.

units.leftText: But because Moses gave you circumcision, you circumcise a boy on the Sabbath (not that it is from Moses, but from the patriarchs.)
units.rightText: Moses hath given you circumcision (not that it is of Moses, but of the fathers); and on the sabbath ye circumcise a man.

units.leftText: If a boy can be circumcised on the Sabbath so that the law of Moses will not be broken, why are you angry with Me for making the whole man well on the Sabbath?
units.rightText: If a man receiveth circumcision on the sabbath, that the law of Moses may not be broken; are ye wroth with me, because I made a man every whit whole on the sabbath?

units.leftText: Stop judging by outward appearances, and start judging justly.” Is Jesus the Christ?
units.rightText: Judge not according to appearance, but judge righteous judgment.

units.leftText: Then some of the people of Jerusalem began to say, “Isn’t this the man they are trying to kill?
units.rightText: Some therefore of them of Jerusalem said, Is not this he whom they seek to kill?

units.leftText: Yet here He is, speaking publicly, and they are not saying anything to Him. Have the rulers truly recognized that this is the Christ?
units.rightText: And lo, he speaketh openly, and they say nothing unto him. Can it be that the rulers indeed know that this is the Christ?

units.leftText: But we know where this man is from. When the Christ comes, no one will know where He is from.”
units.rightText: Howbeit we know this man whence he is: but when the Christ cometh, no one knoweth whence he is.

units.leftText: Then Jesus, still teaching in the temple courts, cried out, “You know Me, and you know where I am from. I have not come of My own accord, but He who sent Me is true. You do not know Him,
units.rightText: Jesus therefore cried in the temple, teaching and saying, Ye both know me, and know whence I am; and I am not come of myself, but he that sent me is true, whom ye know not.

units.leftText: but I know Him, because I am from Him and He sent Me.”
units.rightText: I know him; because I am from him, and he sent me.

units.leftText: So they tried to seize Him, but no one laid a hand on Him, because His hour had not yet come.
units.rightText: They sought therefore to take him: and no man laid his hand on him, because his hour was not yet come.

units.leftText: Many in the crowd, however, believed in Him and said, “When the Christ comes, will He perform more signs than this man?”
units.rightText: But of the multitude many believed on him; and they said, When the Christ shall come, will he do more signs than those which this man hath done?

units.leftText: When the Pharisees heard the crowd whispering these things about Jesus, they and the chief priests sent officers to arrest Him.
