units.rightText: The Pharisees heard the multitude murmuring these things concerning him; and the chief priests and the Pharisees sent officers to take him.

units.leftText: So Jesus said, “I am with you only a little while longer, and then I am going to the One who sent Me.
units.rightText: Jesus therefore said, Yet a little while am I with you, and I go unto him that sent me.

units.leftText: You will look for Me, but you will not find Me; and where I am, you cannot come.”
units.rightText: Ye shall seek me, and shall not find me: and where I am, ye cannot come.

units.leftText: At this, the Jews said to one another, “Where does He intend to go that we will not find Him? Will He go where the Jews are dispersed among the Greeks, and teach the Greeks?
units.rightText: The Jews therefore said among themselves, Whither will this man go that we shall not find him? will he go unto the Dispersion among the Greeks, and teach the Greeks?
leftNotes: 7:35 Literally Will He go to the Diaspora among the Greeks; the Jewish people living outside the land of Israel since the Babylonian exile were referred to as the Diaspora.

units.leftText: What does He mean by saying, ‘You will look for Me, but you will not find Me,’ and, ‘Where I am, you cannot come’?” Living Water
units.rightText: What is this word that he said, Ye shall seek me, and shall not find me; and where I am, ye cannot come?

units.leftText: On the last and greatest day of the feast, Jesus stood up and called out in a loud voice, “If anyone is thirsty, let him come to Me and drink.
units.rightText: Now on the last day, the great day of the feast, Jesus stood and cried, saying, If any man thirst, let him come unto me and drink.

units.leftText: Whoever believes in Me, as the Scripture has said: ‘Streams of living water will flow from within him.’”
units.rightText: He that believeth on me, as the scripture hath said, from within him shall flow rivers of living water.

units.leftText: He was speaking about the Spirit, whom those who believed in Him were later to receive. For the Spirit had not yet been given, because Jesus had not yet been glorified. Division over Jesus
units.rightText: But this spake he of the Spirit, which they that believed on him were to receive: for the Spirit was not yet given; because Jesus was not yet glorified.
leftNotes: 7:39 Literally the Spirit was not yet; BYZ and TR the Holy Spirit was not yet

units.leftText: On hearing these words, some of the people said, “This is truly the Prophet.”
units.rightText: Some of the multitude therefore, when they heard these words, said, This is of a truth the prophet.

units.leftText: Others declared, “This is the Christ.”
units.rightText: Others said, This is the Christ. But some said, What, doth the Christ come out of Galilee?

units.leftText: Doesn’t the Scripture say that the Christ will come from the line of David and from Bethlehem, the village where David lived? ”
units.rightText: Hath not the scripture said that the Christ cometh of the seed of David, and from Bethlehem, the village where David was?
leftNotes: 7:42 See Micah 5:2|MIC 5:2*.

units.leftText: So there was division in the crowd because of Jesus.
units.rightText: So there arose a division in the multitude because of him.

units.leftText: Some of them wanted to seize Him, but no one laid a hand on Him. The Unbelief of the Jewish Leaders
units.rightText: And some of them would have taken him; but no man laid hands on him.

units.leftText: Then the officers returned to the chief priests and Pharisees, who asked them, “Why didn’t you bring Him in?”
units.rightText: The officers therefore came to the chief priests and Pharisees; and they said unto them, Why did ye not bring him?

units.leftText: “Never has anyone spoken like this man!” the officers answered.
units.rightText: The officers answered, Never man so spake.

units.leftText: “Have you also been deceived?” replied the Pharisees.
units.rightText: The Pharisees therefore answered them, Are ye also led astray?

units.leftText: “Have any of the rulers or Pharisees believed in Him?
units.rightText: Hath any of the rulers believed on him, or of the Pharisees?

units.leftText: But this crowd that does not know the law— they are under a curse.”
units.rightText: But this multitude that knoweth not the law are accursed.

units.leftText: Nicodemus, who had gone to Jesus earlier and who himself was one of them, asked,
units.rightText: Nicodemus saith unto them (he that came to him before, being one of them),

units.leftText: “Does our law convict a man without first hearing from him to determine what he has done?”
units.rightText: Doth our law judge a man, except it first hear from himself and know what he doeth?

units.leftText: “Aren’t you also from Galilee?” they replied. “Look into it, and you will see that no prophet comes out of Galilee.”
units.rightText: They answered and said unto him, Art thou also of Galilee? Search, and see that out of Galilee ariseth no prophet.
leftNotes: 7:52 Some early manuscripts do not include John 7:53|JHN 7:53* through John 8:11.

units.leftText: Then each went to his own home.
units.rightText: [And they went every man unto his own house:

units.leftText: But Jesus went to the Mount of Olives.
units.rightText: but Jesus went unto the mount of Olives.

units.leftText: Early in the morning He went back into the temple courts. All the people came to Him, and He sat down to teach them.
units.rightText: And early in the morning he came again into the temple, and all the people came unto him; and he sat down, and taught them.
leftNotes: 8:2 Literally the temple; also in verse 20

units.leftText: The scribes and Pharisees, however, brought to Him a woman caught in adultery. They made her stand before them
units.rightText: And the scribes and the Pharisees bring a woman taken in adultery; and having set her in the midst,

units.leftText: and said, “Teacher, this woman was caught in the act of adultery.
units.rightText: they say unto him, Teacher, this woman hath been taken in adultery, in the very act.

units.leftText: In the Law Moses commanded us to stone such a woman. So what do You say?”
units.rightText: Now in the law Moses commanded us to stone such: what then sayest thou of her?

units.leftText: They said this to test Him, in order to have a basis for accusing Him. But Jesus bent down and began to write on the ground with His finger.
units.rightText: And this they said, trying him, that they might have whereof to accuse him. But Jesus stooped down, and with his finger wrote on the ground.

units.leftText: When they continued to question Him, He straightened up and said to them, “Let him who is without sin among you be the first to cast a stone at her.”
units.rightText: But when they continued asking him, he lifted up himself, and said unto them, He that is without sin among you, let him first cast a stone at her.

units.leftText: And again He bent down and wrote on the ground.
units.rightText: And again he stooped down, and with his finger wrote on the ground.

units.leftText: When they heard this, they began to go away one by one, beginning with the older ones, until only Jesus was left, with the woman standing there.
units.rightText: And they, when they heard it, went out one by one, beginning from the eldest, even unto the last: and Jesus was left alone, and the woman, where she was, in the midst.
leftNotes: 8:9 NE, BYZ, and TR include and were convicted by their conscience,

units.leftText: Then Jesus straightened up and asked her, “Woman, where are your accusers? Has no one condemned you?”
units.rightText: And Jesus lifted up himself, and said unto her, Woman, where are they? did no man condemn thee?
leftNotes: 8:10 NE, BYZ, and TR include and saw no one but the woman.
8:10 WH and NA where are they

units.leftText: “No one, Lord,” she answered. “Then neither do I condemn you,” Jesus declared. “Now go and sin no more.” Jesus the Light of the World (1 John 1:5–10|1JN 1:5-10*)
units.rightText: And she said, No man, Lord. And Jesus said, Neither do I condemn thee: go thy way; from henceforth sin no more.]

units.leftText: Once again, Jesus spoke to the people and said, “I am the light of the world. Whoever follows Me will never walk in the darkness, but will have the light of life.”
units.rightText: Again therefore Jesus spake unto them, saying, I am the light of the world: he that followeth me shall not walk in the darkness, but shall have the light of life.

units.leftText: So the Pharisees said to Him, “You are testifying about Yourself; Your testimony is not valid.”
units.rightText: The Pharisees therefore said unto him, Thou bearest witness of thyself; thy witness is not true.

units.leftText: Jesus replied, “Even if I testify about Myself, My testimony is valid, because I know where I came from and where I am going. But you do not know where I came from or where I am going.
units.rightText: Jesus answered and said unto them, Even if I bear witness of myself, my witness is true; for I know whence I came, and whither I go; but ye know not whence I come, or whither I go.

units.leftText: You judge according to the flesh; I judge no one.
units.rightText: Ye judge after the flesh; I judge no man.

units.leftText: But even if I do judge, My judgment is true, because I am not alone; I am with the Father who sent Me.
units.rightText: Yea and if I judge, my judgment is true; for I am not alone, but I and the Father that sent me.
leftNotes: 8:16 Literally but (it is) I and the Father who sent Me; NE but (it is) I and the One who sent Me

units.leftText: Even in your own Law it is written that the testimony of two men is valid.
units.rightText: Yea and in your law it is written, that the witness of two men is true.
leftNotes: 8:17 See Deuteronomy 19:15|DEU 19:15*.

units.leftText: I am One who testifies about Myself, and the Father, who sent Me, also testifies about Me.”
units.rightText: I am he that beareth witness of myself, and the Father that sent me beareth witness of me.

units.leftText: “Where is Your Father?” they asked Him. “You do not know Me or My Father,” Jesus answered. “If you knew Me, you would know My Father as well.”
units.rightText: They said therefore unto him, Where is thy Father? Jesus answered, Ye know neither me, nor my Father: if ye knew me, ye would know my Father also.

units.leftText: He spoke these words while teaching in the temple courts, near the treasury. Yet no one seized Him, because His hour had not yet come.
units.rightText: These words spake he in the treasury, as he taught in the temple: and no man took him; because his hour was not yet come.

units.leftText: Again He said to them, “I am going away, and you will look for Me, but you will die in your sin. Where I am going, you cannot come.”
units.rightText: He said therefore again unto them, I go away, and ye shall seek me, and shall die in your sin: whither I go, ye cannot come.

units.leftText: So the Jews began to ask, “Will He kill Himself, since He says, ‘Where I am going, you cannot come’?”
units.rightText: The Jews therefore said, Will he kill himself, that he saith, Whither I go, ye cannot come?

units.leftText: Then He told them, “You are from below; I am from above. You are of this world; I am not of this world.
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Ye are from beneath; I am from above: ye are of this world; I am not of this world.

units.leftText: That is why I told you that you would die in your sins. For unless you believe that I am He, you will die in your sins.”
units.rightText: I said therefore unto you, that ye shall die in your sins: for except ye believe that I am he, ye shall die in your sins.

units.leftText: “Who are You?” they asked.
units.rightText: They said therefore unto him, Who art thou? Jesus said unto them, Even that which I have also spoken unto you from the beginning.

units.leftText: “I have much to say about you and much to judge. But the One who sent Me is truthful, and what I have heard from Him, I tell the world.”
units.rightText: I have many things to speak and to judge concerning you: howbeit he that sent me is true; and the things which I heard from him, these speak I unto the world.

units.leftText: They did not understand that He was telling them about the Father.
units.rightText: They perceived not that he spake to them of the Father.

units.leftText: So Jesus said, “When you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will know that I am He, and that I do nothing on My own, but speak exactly what the Father has taught Me.
units.rightText: Jesus therefore said, When ye have lifted up the Son of man, then shall ye know that I am he, and that I do nothing of myself, but as the Father taught me, I speak these things.

units.leftText: He who sent Me is with Me. He has not left Me alone, because I always do what pleases Him.” The Truth Will Set You Free (2 John 1:4–6|2JN 4-6*)
units.rightText: And he that sent me is with me; he hath not left me alone; for I do always the things that are pleasing to him.

units.leftText: As Jesus spoke these things, many believed in Him.
units.rightText: As he spake these things, many believed on him.

units.leftText: So He said to the Jews who had believed Him, “If you continue in My word, you are truly My disciples.
units.rightText: Jesus therefore said to those Jews that had believed him, If ye abide in my word, then are ye truly my disciples;

units.leftText: Then you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free.”
units.rightText: and ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.

units.leftText: “We are Abraham’s descendants,” they answered. “We have never been slaves to anyone. How can You say we will be set free?”
units.rightText: They answered unto him, We are Abraham’s seed, and have never yet been in bondage to any man: how sayest thou, Ye shall be made free?

units.leftText: Jesus replied, “Truly, truly, I tell you, everyone who sins is a slave to sin.
units.rightText: Jesus answered them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Every one that committeth sin is the bondservant of sin.

units.leftText: A slave does not remain in the house forever, but a son remains forever.
units.rightText: And the bondservant abideth not in the house for ever: the son abideth for ever.

units.leftText: So if the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed.
units.rightText: If therefore the Son shall make you free, ye shall be free indeed.

units.leftText: I know you are Abraham’s descendants, but you are trying to kill Me because My word has no place within you.
units.rightText: I know that ye are Abraham’s seed; yet ye seek to kill me, because my word hath not free course in you.

units.leftText: I speak of what I have seen in the presence of the Father, and you do what you have heard from your father.”
units.rightText: I speak the things which I have seen with my Father: and ye also do the things which ye heard from your father.

units.leftText: “Abraham is our father,” they replied.
units.rightText: They answered and said unto him, Our father is Abraham. Jesus saith unto them, If ye were Abraham’s children, ye would do the works of Abraham.

units.leftText: But now you are trying to kill Me, a man who has told you the truth that I heard from God. Abraham never did such a thing.
units.rightText: But now ye seek to kill me, a man that hath told you the truth, which I heard from God: this did not Abraham.

units.leftText: You are doing the works of your father.” “We are not illegitimate children,” they declared. “Our only Father is God Himself.”
units.rightText: Ye do the works of your father. They said unto him, We were not born of fornication; we have one Father, even God.

units.leftText: Jesus said to them, “If God were your Father, you would love Me, for I have come here from God. I have not come on My own, but He sent Me.
units.rightText: Jesus said unto them, If God were your Father, ye would love me: for I came forth and am come from God; for neither have I come of myself, but he sent me.

units.leftText: Why do you not understand what I am saying? It is because you are unable to accept My message.
units.rightText: Why do ye not understand my speech? Even because ye cannot hear my word.

units.leftText: You belong to your father, the devil, and you want to carry out his desires. He was a murderer from the beginning, refusing to uphold the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he lies, he speaks his native language, because he is a liar and the father of lies.
units.rightText: Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father it is your will to do. He was a murderer from the beginning, and standeth not in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaketh a lie, he speaketh of his own: for he is a liar, and the father thereof.

units.leftText: But because I speak the truth, you do not believe Me!
units.rightText: But because I say the truth, ye believe me not.

units.leftText: Which of you can prove Me guilty of sin? If I speak the truth, why do you not believe Me?
units.rightText: Which of you convicteth me of sin? If I say truth, why do ye not believe me?

units.leftText: Whoever belongs to God hears the words of God. The reason you do not hear is that you do not belong to God.” Before Abraham Was Born, I Am
units.rightText: He that is of God heareth the words of God: for this cause ye hear them not, because ye are not of God.

units.leftText: The Jews answered Him, “Are we not right to say that You are a Samaritan and You have a demon?”
units.rightText: The Jews answered and said unto him, Say we not well that thou art a Samaritan, and hast a demon?

units.leftText: “I do not have a demon,” Jesus replied, “but I honor My Father, and you dishonor Me.
units.rightText: Jesus answered, I have not a demon; but I honor my Father, and ye dishonor me.

units.leftText: I do not seek My own glory. There is One who seeks it, and He is the Judge.
units.rightText: But I seek not mine own glory: there is one that seeketh and judgeth.

units.leftText: Truly, truly, I tell you, if anyone keeps My word, he will never see death.”
units.rightText: Verily, verily, I say unto you, If a man keep my word, he shall never see death.

units.leftText: “Now we know that You have a demon!” declared the Jews. “Abraham died, and so did the prophets, yet You say that anyone who keeps Your word will never taste death.
units.rightText: The Jews said unto him, Now we know that thou hast a demon. Abraham died, and the prophets; and thou sayest, If a man keep my word, he shall never taste of death.

units.leftText: Are You greater than our father Abraham? He died, as did the prophets. Who do You claim to be?”
units.rightText: Art thou greater than our father Abraham, who died? and the prophets died: whom makest thou thyself?

units.leftText: Jesus answered, “If I glorify Myself, My glory means nothing. The One who glorifies Me is My Father, of whom you say, ‘He is our God.’
units.rightText: Jesus answered, If I glorify myself, my glory is nothing: it is my Father that glorifieth me; of whom ye say, that he is your God;
leftNotes: 8:54 WH and TR Your

units.leftText: You do not know Him, but I know Him. If I said I did not know Him, I would be a liar like you. But I do know Him, and I keep His word.
units.rightText: and ye have not known him: but I know him; and if I should say, I know him not, I shall be like unto you, a liar: but I know him, and keep his word.

units.leftText: Your father Abraham rejoiced that he would see My day. He saw it and was glad.”
units.rightText: Your father Abraham rejoiced to see my day; and he saw it, and was glad.

units.leftText: Then the Jews said to Him, “You are not yet fifty years old, and You have seen Abraham?”
units.rightText: The Jews therefore said unto him, Thou art not yet fifty years old, and hast thou seen Abraham?

units.leftText: “Truly, truly, I tell you,” Jesus declared, “before Abraham was born, I am! ”
units.rightText: Jesus said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Before Abraham was born, I am.
leftNotes: 8:58 Literally before Abraham was, I am!

units.leftText: At this, they picked up stones to throw at Him. But Jesus was hidden and went out of the temple area.
units.rightText: They took up stones therefore to cast at him: but Jesus hid himself, and went out of the temple.
leftNotes: 8:59 BYZ and TR include going through the midst of them, and so He passed by.

units.leftText: Now as Jesus was passing by, He saw a man blind from birth,
units.rightText: And as he passed by, he saw a man blind from his birth.

units.leftText: and His disciples asked Him, “Rabbi, who sinned, this man or his parents, that he was born blind?”
units.rightText: And his disciples asked him, saying, Rabbi, who sinned, this man, or his parents, that he should be born blind?

units.leftText: Jesus answered, “Neither this man nor his parents sinned, but this happened so that the works of God would be displayed in him.
units.rightText: Jesus answered, Neither did this man sin, nor his parents: but that the works of God should be made manifest in him.

units.leftText: While it is daytime, we must do the works of Him who sent Me. Night is coming, when no one can work.
units.rightText: We must work the works of him that sent me, while it is day: the night cometh, when no man can work.
leftNotes: 9:4 BYZ and TR I must do

units.leftText: While I am in the world, I am the light of the world.”
units.rightText: When I am in the world, I am the light of the world.

units.leftText: When Jesus had said this, He spit on the ground, made some mud, and applied it to the man’s eyes.
units.rightText: When he had thus spoken, he spat on the ground, and made clay of the spittle, and anointed his eyes with the clay,

units.leftText: Then He told him, “Go, wash in the Pool of Siloam” (which means “Sent”). So the man went and washed, and came back seeing.
units.rightText: and said unto him, Go, wash in the pool of Siloam (which is by interpretation, Sent). He went away therefore, and washed, and came seeing.

units.leftText: At this, his neighbors and those who had formerly seen him begging began to ask, “Isn’t this the man who used to sit and beg?”
units.rightText: The neighbors therefore, and they that saw him aforetime, that he was a beggar, said, Is not this he that sat and begged?

units.leftText: Some claimed that he was, but others said, “No, he just looks like him.” But the man kept saying, “I am the one.”
units.rightText: Others said, It is he: others said, No, but he is like him. He said, I am he.

units.leftText: “How then were your eyes opened?” they asked.
units.rightText: They said therefore unto him, How then were thine eyes opened?

units.leftText: He answered, “The man they call Jesus made some mud and anointed my eyes, and He told me to go to Siloam and wash. So I went and washed and received my sight.”
units.rightText: He answered, The man that is called Jesus made clay, and anointed mine eyes, and said unto me, Go to Siloam, and wash: so I went away and washed, and I received sight.

units.leftText: “Where is He?” they asked. “I do not know,” he answered. The Pharisees Investigate the Healing
units.rightText: And they said unto him, Where is he? He saith, I know not.

units.leftText: They brought to the Pharisees the man who had been blind.
units.rightText: They bring to the Pharisees him that aforetime was blind.

units.leftText: Now the day on which Jesus had made the mud and opened his eyes was a Sabbath.
units.rightText: Now it was the sabbath on the day when Jesus made the clay, and opened his eyes.

units.leftText: So the Pharisees also asked him how he had received his sight. The man answered, “He put mud on my eyes, and I washed, and now I can see.”
units.rightText: Again therefore the Pharisees also asked him how he received his sight. And he said unto them, He put clay upon mine eyes, and I washed, and I see.

units.leftText: Because of this, some of the Pharisees said, “This man is not from God, for He does not keep the Sabbath.” But others said, “How can a sinful man perform such signs?”
units.rightText: Some therefore of the Pharisees said, This man is not from God, because he keepeth not the sabbath. But others said, How can a man that is a sinner do such signs? And there was a division among them.

units.leftText: So once again they asked the man who had been blind, “What do you say about Him, since it was your eyes He opened?” “He is a prophet,” the man replied.
units.rightText: They say therefore unto the blind man again, What sayest thou of him, in that he opened thine eyes? And he said, He is a prophet.

units.leftText: The Jews still did not believe that the man had been blind and had received his sight until they summoned his parents
units.rightText: The Jews therefore did not believe concerning him, that he had been blind, and had received his sight, until they called the parents of him that had received his sight,

units.leftText: and asked, “Is this your son, the one you say was born blind? So how is it that he can now see?”
units.rightText: and asked them, saying, Is this your son, who ye say was born blind? how then doth he now see?

units.leftText: His parents answered, “We know he is our son, and we know he was born blind.
units.rightText: His parents answered and said, We know that this is our son, and that he was born blind:

units.leftText: But how he can now see or who opened his eyes, we do not know. Ask him. He is old enough to speak for himself.”
units.rightText: but how he now seeth, we know not; or who opened his eyes, we know not: ask him; he is of age; he shall speak for himself.

units.leftText: His parents said this because they were afraid of the Jews. For the Jews had already determined that anyone who confessed Jesus as the Christ would be put out of the synagogue.
units.rightText: These things said his parents, because they feared the Jews: for the Jews had agreed already, that if any man should confess him to be Christ, he should be put out of the synagogue.

units.leftText: That was why his parents said, “He is old enough. Ask him.”
units.rightText: Therefore said his parents, He is of age; ask him.

units.leftText: So a second time they called for the man who had been blind and said, “Give glory to God! We know that this man is a sinner.”
units.rightText: So they called a second time the man that was blind, and said unto him, Give glory to God: we know that this man is a sinner.

units.leftText: He answered, “Whether He is a sinner I do not know. There is one thing I do know: I was blind, but now I see!”
units.rightText: He therefore answered, Whether he is a sinner, I know not: one thing I know, that, whereas I was blind, now I see.

units.leftText: “What did He do to you?” they asked. “How did He open your eyes?”
units.rightText: They said therefore unto him, What did he to thee? how opened he thine eyes?

units.leftText: He replied, “I already told you, and you did not listen. Why do you want to hear it again? Do you also want to become His disciples?”
units.rightText: He answered them, I told you even now, and ye did not hear; wherefore would ye hear it again? would ye also become his disciples?

units.leftText: Then they heaped insults on him and said, “You are His disciple; we are disciples of Moses.
units.rightText: And they reviled him, and said, Thou art his disciple; but we are disciples of Moses.

units.leftText: We know that God spoke to Moses, but we do not know where this man is from.”
units.rightText: We know that God hath spoken unto Moses: but as for this man, we know not whence he is.

units.leftText: “That is remarkable indeed!” the man said. “You do not know where He is from, and yet He opened my eyes.
units.rightText: The man answered and said unto them, Why, herein is the marvel, that ye know not whence he is, and yet he opened mine eyes.

units.leftText: We know that God does not listen to sinners, but He does listen to the one who worships Him and does His will.
units.rightText: We know that God heareth not sinners: but if any man be a worshipper of God, and do his will, him he heareth.

units.leftText: Never before has anyone heard of opening the eyes of a man born blind.
units.rightText: Since the world began it was never heard that any one opened the eyes of a man born blind.

units.leftText: If this man were not from God, He could do no such thing.”
units.rightText: If this man were not from God, he could do nothing.

units.leftText: They replied, “You were born in utter sin, and you are instructing us?” And they threw him out. Spiritual Blindness
units.rightText: They answered and said unto him, Thou wast altogether born in sins, and dost thou teach us? And they cast him out.

units.leftText: When Jesus heard that they had thrown him out, He found the man and said, “Do you believe in the Son of Man ?”
units.rightText: Jesus heard that they had cast him out; and finding him, he said, Dost thou believe on the Son of God?
leftNotes: 9:35 BYZ and TR the Son of God

units.leftText: “Who is He, Sir?” he replied. “Tell me so that I may believe in Him.”
units.rightText: He answered and said, And who is he, Lord, that I may believe on him?

units.leftText: “You have already seen Him,” Jesus answered. “He is the One speaking with you.”
units.rightText: Jesus said unto him, Thou hast both seen him, and he it is that speaketh with thee.

units.leftText: “Lord, I believe,” he said. And he worshiped Jesus.
units.rightText: And he said, Lord, I believe. And he worshipped him.

units.leftText: Then Jesus declared, “For judgment I have come into this world, so that the blind may see and those who see may become blind.”
units.rightText: And Jesus said, For judgment came I into this world, that they that see not may see; and that they that see may become blind.
leftNotes: 9:39 Literally so that those not seeing may see and those seeing may become blind. Some manuscripts do not include 38*“Lord, I believe.”... 39*Then Jesus declared.

units.leftText: Some of the Pharisees who were with Him heard this, and they asked Him, “Are we blind too?”
units.rightText: Those of the Pharisees who were with him heard these things, and said unto him, Are we also blind?

units.leftText: “If you were blind,” Jesus replied, “you would not be guilty of sin. But since you claim you can see, your guilt remains.”
units.rightText: Jesus said unto them, If ye were blind, ye would have no sin: but now ye say, We see: your sin remaineth.

units.leftText: “Truly, truly, I tell you, whoever does not enter the sheepfold by the gate, but climbs in some other way, is a thief and a robber.
units.rightText: Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that entereth not by the door into the fold of the sheep, but climbeth up some other way, the same is a thief and a robber.

units.leftText: But the one who enters by the gate is the shepherd of the sheep.
units.rightText: But he that entereth in by the door is the shepherd of the sheep.

units.leftText: The gatekeeper opens the gate for him, and the sheep listen for his voice. He calls his own sheep by name and leads them out.
units.rightText: To him the porter openeth; and the sheep hear his voice: and he calleth his own sheep by name, and leadeth them out.

units.leftText: When he has brought out all his own, he goes on ahead of them, and his sheep follow him because they know his voice.
units.rightText: When he hath put forth all his own, he goeth before them, and the sheep follow him: for they know his voice.

units.leftText: But they will never follow a stranger; in fact, they will flee from him because they do not recognize his voice.”
units.rightText: And a stranger will they not follow, but will flee from him: for they know not the voice of strangers.

units.leftText: Jesus spoke to them using this illustration, but they did not understand what He was telling them.
units.rightText: This parable spake Jesus unto them: but they understood not what things they were which he spake unto them.

units.leftText: So He said to them again, “Truly, truly, I tell you, I am the gate for the sheep.
units.rightText: Jesus therefore said unto them again, Verily, verily, I say unto you, I am the door of the sheep.

units.leftText: All who came before Me were thieves and robbers, but the sheep did not listen to them.
units.rightText: All that came before me are thieves and robbers: but the sheep did not hear them.
leftNotes: 10:8 BYZ All who came

units.leftText: I am the gate. If anyone enters through Me, he will be saved. He will come in and go out and find pasture.
units.rightText: I am the door; by me if any man enter in, he shall be saved, and shall go in and go out, and shall find pasture.

units.leftText: The thief comes only to steal and kill and destroy. I have come that they may have life, and have it in all its fullness.
units.rightText: The thief cometh not, but that he may steal, and kill, and destroy: I came that they may have life, and may have it abundantly.

units.leftText: I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down His life for the sheep.
units.rightText: I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd layeth down his life for the sheep.

units.leftText: The hired hand is not the shepherd, and the sheep are not his own. When he sees the wolf coming, he abandons the sheep and runs away. Then the wolf pounces on them and scatters the flock.
units.rightText: He that is a hireling, and not a shepherd, whose own the sheep are not, beholdeth the wolf coming, and leaveth the sheep, and fleeth, and the wolf snatcheth them, and scattereth them:

units.leftText: The man runs away because he is a hired servant and is unconcerned for the sheep.
units.rightText: he fleeth because he is a hireling, and careth not for the sheep.

units.leftText: I am the good shepherd. I know My sheep and My sheep know Me,
units.rightText: I am the good shepherd; and I know mine own, and mine own know me,

units.leftText: just as the Father knows Me and I know the Father. And I lay down My life for the sheep.
units.rightText: even as the Father knoweth me, and I know the Father; and I lay down my life for the sheep.

units.leftText: I have other sheep that are not of this fold. I must bring them in as well, and they will listen to My voice. Then there will be one flock and one shepherd.
units.rightText: And other sheep I have, which are not of this fold: them also I must bring, and they shall hear my voice; and they shall become one flock, one shepherd.

units.leftText: The reason the Father loves Me is that I lay down My life in order to take it up again.
units.rightText: Therefore doth the Father love me, because I lay down my life, that I may take it again.

units.leftText: No one takes it from Me, but I lay it down of My own accord. I have authority to lay it down and authority to take it up again. This charge I have received from My Father.”
units.rightText: No one taketh it away from me, but I lay it down of myself. I have power to lay it down, and I have power to take it again. This commandment received I from my Father.

units.leftText: Again there was division among the Jews because of Jesus’ message.
units.rightText: There arose a division again among the Jews because of these words.

units.leftText: Many of them said, “He is demon-possessed and insane. Why would you listen to Him?”
units.rightText: And many of them said, He hath a demon, and is mad; why hear ye him?

units.leftText: But others replied, “These are not the words of a man possessed by a demon. Can a demon open the eyes of the blind?” Jesus at the Feast of Dedication
units.rightText: Others said, These are not the sayings of one possessed with a demon. Can a demon open the eyes of the blind?

units.leftText: So the Jews gathered around Him and demanded, “How long will You keep us in suspense? If You are the Christ, tell us plainly.”
units.rightText: The Jews therefore came round about him, and said unto him, How long dost thou hold us in suspense? If thou art the Christ, tell us plainly.

units.leftText: “I already told you,” Jesus replied, “but you did not believe. The works I do in My Father’s name testify on My behalf.
units.rightText: Jesus answered them, I told you, and ye believe not: the works that I do in my Father’s name, these bear witness of me.

units.leftText: But because you are not My sheep, you refuse to believe.
units.rightText: But ye believe not, because ye are not of my sheep.

units.leftText: My sheep listen to My voice; I know them, and they follow Me.
units.rightText: My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me:

units.leftText: I give them eternal life, and they will never perish. No one can snatch them out of My hand.
units.rightText: and I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish, and no one shall snatch them out of my hand.

units.leftText: My Father who has given them to Me is greater than all. No one can snatch them out of My Father’s hand.
units.rightText: My Father, who hath given them unto me, is greater than all; and no one is able to snatch them out of the Father’s hand.

units.leftText: I and the Father are one.”
units.rightText: I and the Father are one.

units.leftText: At this, the Jews again picked up stones to stone Him.
units.rightText: The Jews took up stones again to stone him.

units.leftText: But Jesus responded, “I have shown you many good works from the Father. For which of these do you stone Me?”
units.rightText: Jesus answered them, Many good works have I showed you from the Father; for which of those works do ye stone me?

units.leftText: “We are not stoning You for any good work,” said the Jews, “but for blasphemy, because You, who are a man, make Yourself out to be God.”
units.rightText: The Jews answered him, For a good work we stone thee not, but for blasphemy; and because that thou, being a man, makest thyself God.

units.leftText: Jesus replied, “Is it not written in your Law: ‘I have said you are gods’ ?
units.rightText: Jesus answered them, Is it not written in your law, I said, Ye are gods?

units.leftText: If he called them gods to whom the word of God came — and the Scripture cannot be broken —
units.rightText: If he called them gods, unto whom the word of God came (and the scripture cannot be broken),

units.rightText: say ye of him, whom the Father sanctified and sent into the world, Thou blasphemest; because I said, I am the Son of God?

units.leftText: If I am not doing the works of My Father, then do not believe Me.
units.rightText: If I do not the works of my Father, believe me not.

units.leftText: But if I am doing them, even though you do not believe Me, believe the works themselves, so that you may know and understand that the Father is in Me, and I am in the Father.”
units.rightText: But if I do them, though ye believe not me, believe the works: that ye may know and understand that the Father is in me, and I in the Father.

units.leftText: At this, they tried again to seize Him, but He escaped their grasp. John’s Testimony Confirmed
units.rightText: They sought again to take him: and he went forth out of their hand.

units.leftText: Then Jesus went back across the Jordan to the place where John had first been baptizing, and He stayed there.
units.rightText: And he went away again beyond the Jordan into the place where John was at the first baptizing; and there he abode.

units.leftText: Many came to Him and said, “Although John never performed a sign, everything he said about this man was true.”
units.rightText: And many came unto him; and they said, John indeed did no sign: but all things whatsoever John spake of this man were true.

units.leftText: And many in that place believed in Jesus.
units.rightText: And many believed on him there.

units.leftText: At this time a man named Lazarus was sick. He lived in Bethany, the village of Mary and her sister Martha.
units.rightText: Now a certain man was sick, Lazarus of Bethany, of the village of Mary and her sister Martha.

units.leftText: (Mary, whose brother Lazarus was sick, was to anoint the Lord with perfume and wipe His feet with her hair.)
units.rightText: And it was that Mary who anointed the Lord with ointment, and wiped his feet with her hair, whose brother Lazarus was sick.
leftNotes: 11:2 Literally was the one having anointed the Lord with fragrant oil and having wiped His feet; see John 12:3|JHN 12:3*.

units.leftText: So the sisters sent word to Jesus, “Lord, the one You love is sick.”
units.rightText: The sisters therefore sent unto him, saying, Lord, behold, he whom thou lovest is sick.

units.leftText: When Jesus heard this, He said, “This sickness will not end in death. No, it is for the glory of God, so that the Son of God may be glorified through it.”
units.rightText: But when Jesus heard it, he said, This sickness is not unto death, but for the glory of God, that the Son of God may be glorified thereby.

units.leftText: Now Jesus loved Martha and her sister and Lazarus.
units.rightText: Now Jesus loved Martha, and her sister, and Lazarus.

units.leftText: So on hearing that Lazarus was sick, He stayed where He was for two days,
units.rightText: When therefore he heard that he was sick, he abode at that time two days in the place where he was.

units.leftText: and then He said to the disciples, “Let us go back to Judea.”
units.rightText: Then after this he saith to the disciples, Let us go into Judæa again.

units.leftText: “Rabbi,” they replied, “the Jews just tried to stone You, and You are going back there?”
units.rightText: The disciples say unto him, Rabbi, the Jews were but now seeking to stone thee; and goest thou thither again?

units.leftText: Jesus answered, “Are there not twelve hours of daylight? If anyone walks in the daytime, he will not stumble, because he sees by the light of this world.
units.rightText: Jesus answered, Are there not twelve hours in the day? If a man walk in the day, he stumbleth not, because he seeth the light of this world.

units.leftText: But if anyone walks at night, he will stumble, because he has no light.”
units.rightText: But if a man walk in the night, he stumbleth, because the light is not in him.

units.leftText: After He had said this, He told them, “Our friend Lazarus has fallen asleep, but I am going there to wake him up.”
units.rightText: These things spake he: and after this he saith unto them, Our friend Lazarus is fallen asleep; but I go, that I may awake him out of sleep.

units.leftText: His disciples replied, “Lord, if he is sleeping, he will get better.”
units.rightText: The disciples therefore said unto him, Lord, if he is fallen asleep, he will recover.

units.leftText: They thought that Jesus was talking about actual sleep, but He was speaking about the death of Lazarus.
units.rightText: Now Jesus had spoken of his death: but they thought that he spake of taking rest in sleep.

units.leftText: So Jesus told them plainly, “Lazarus is dead,
units.rightText: Then Jesus therefore said unto them plainly, Lazarus is dead.

units.leftText: and for your sake I am glad I was not there, so that you may believe. But let us go to him.”
units.rightText: And I am glad for your sakes that I was not there, to the intent ye may believe; nevertheless let us go unto him.

units.leftText: Then Thomas called Didymus said to his fellow disciples, “Let us also go, so that we may die with Him.” Jesus Comforts Martha and Mary
units.rightText: Thomas therefore, who is called Didymus, said unto his fellow-disciples, Let us also go, that we may die with him.
leftNotes: 11:16 Didymus means the twin.

units.leftText: When Jesus arrived, He found that Lazarus had already spent four days in the tomb.
units.rightText: So when Jesus came, he found that he had been in the tomb four days already.

units.leftText: Now Bethany was near Jerusalem, a little less than two miles away,
units.rightText: Now Bethany was nigh unto Jerusalem, about fifteen furlongs off;
leftNotes: 11:18 Greek about fifteen stadia; that is, approximately 1.72 miles or 2.78 kilometers

units.leftText: and many of the Jews had come to Martha and Mary to console them in the loss of their brother.
units.rightText: and many of the Jews had come to Martha and Mary, to console them concerning their brother.

units.leftText: So when Martha heard that Jesus was coming, she went out to meet Him, but Mary stayed at home.
units.rightText: Martha therefore, when she heard that Jesus was coming, went and met him: but Mary still sat in the house.

units.leftText: Martha said to Jesus, “Lord, if You had been here, my brother would not have died.
units.rightText: Martha therefore said unto Jesus, Lord, if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died.

units.leftText: But even now I know that God will give You whatever You ask of Him.”
units.rightText: And even now I know that, whatsoever thou shalt ask of God, God will give thee.

units.leftText: “Your brother will rise again,” Jesus told her.
units.rightText: Jesus saith unto her, Thy brother shall rise again.

units.leftText: Martha replied, “I know that he will rise again in the resurrection at the last day.”
units.rightText: Martha saith unto him, I know that he shall rise again in the resurrection at the last day.

units.leftText: Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in Me will live, even though he dies.
units.rightText: Jesus said unto her, I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth on me, though he die, yet shall he live;

units.leftText: And everyone who lives and believes in Me will never die. Do you believe this?”
units.rightText: and whosoever liveth and believeth on me shall never die. Believest thou this?

units.leftText: “Yes, Lord,” she answered, “I believe that You are the Christ, the Son of God, who was to come into the world.”
units.rightText: She saith unto him, Yea, Lord: I have believed that thou art the Christ, the Son of God, even he that cometh into the world.

units.leftText: After Martha had said this, she went back and called her sister Mary aside to tell her, “The Teacher is here and is asking for you.”
units.rightText: And when she had said this, she went away, and called Mary her sister secretly, saying, The Teacher is here, and calleth thee.

units.leftText: And when Mary heard this, she got up quickly and went to Him.
units.rightText: And she, when she heard it, arose quickly, and went unto him.

units.leftText: Now Jesus had not yet entered the village, but was still at the place where Martha had met Him.
units.rightText: (Now Jesus was not yet come into the village, but was still in the place where Martha met him.)

units.leftText: When the Jews who were in the house consoling Mary saw how quickly she got up and went out, they followed her, supposing she was going to the tomb to mourn there.
units.rightText: The Jews then who were with her in the house, and were consoling her, when they saw Mary, that she rose up quickly and went out, followed her, supposing that she was going unto the tomb to weep there.

units.leftText: When Mary came to Jesus and saw Him, she fell at His feet and said, “Lord, if You had been here, my brother would not have died.”
units.rightText: Mary therefore, when she came where Jesus was, and saw him, fell down at his feet, saying unto him, Lord, if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died.

units.leftText: When Jesus saw her weeping, and the Jews who had come with her also weeping, He was deeply moved in spirit and troubled.
units.rightText: When Jesus therefore saw her weeping, and the Jews also weeping who came with her, he groaned in the spirit, and was troubled,
leftNotes: 11:33 Or He was indignant in spirit; similarly in verse 38

units.leftText: “Where have you put him?” He asked. “Come and see, Lord,” they answered.
units.rightText: and said, Where have ye laid him? They say unto him, Lord, come and see.

units.leftText: Jesus wept.
units.rightText: Jesus wept.

units.leftText: Then the Jews said, “See how He loved him!”
units.rightText: The Jews therefore said, Behold how he loved him!

units.leftText: But some of them asked, “Could not this man who opened the eyes of the blind also have kept Lazarus from dying?” Jesus Raises Lazarus (Acts 9:36–43|ACT 9:36-43*)
units.rightText: But some of them said, Could not this man, who opened the eyes of him that was blind, have caused that this man also should not die?

units.leftText: Jesus, once again deeply moved, came to the tomb. It was a cave with a stone laid across the entrance.
units.rightText: Jesus therefore again groaning in himself cometh to the tomb. Now it was a cave, and a stone lay against it.

units.leftText: “Take away the stone,” Jesus said. “Lord, by now he stinks,” said Martha, the sister of the dead man. “It has already been four days.”
units.rightText: Jesus saith, Take ye away the stone. Martha, the sister of him that was dead, saith unto him, Lord, by this time the body decayeth; for he hath been dead four days.

units.leftText: Jesus replied, “Did I not tell you that if you believed, you would see the glory of God?”
units.rightText: Jesus saith unto her, Said I not unto thee, that, if thou believedst, thou shouldest see the glory of God?

units.leftText: So they took away the stone. Then Jesus lifted His eyes upward and said, “Father, I thank You that You have heard Me.
units.rightText: So they took away the stone. And Jesus lifted up his eyes, and said, Father, I thank thee that thou heardest me.

units.leftText: I knew that You always hear Me, but I say this for the benefit of the people standing here, so they may believe that You sent Me.”
units.rightText: And I knew that thou hearest me always: but because of the multitude that standeth around I said it, that they may believe that thou didst send me.

units.leftText: After Jesus had said this, He called out in a loud voice, “Lazarus, come out!”
units.rightText: And when he had thus spoken, he cried with a loud voice, Lazarus, come forth.

units.leftText: The man who had been dead came out with his hands and feet bound in strips of linen, and his face wrapped in a cloth. “Unwrap him and let him go,” Jesus told them. The Plot to Kill Jesus (Matthew 26:1–5|MAT 26:1-5*; Mark 14:1–2|MRK 14:1-2*; Luke 22:1–2|LUK 22:1-2*)
units.rightText: He that was dead came forth, bound hand and foot with grave-clothes; and his face was bound about with a napkin. Jesus saith unto them, Loose him, and let him go.
leftNotes: 11:44 Greek soudariō

units.leftText: Therefore many of the Jews who had come to Mary, and had seen what Jesus did, believed in Him.
units.rightText: Many therefore of the Jews, who came to Mary and beheld that which he did, believed on him.

units.leftText: But some of them went to the Pharisees and told them what Jesus had done.
units.rightText: But some of them went away to the Pharisees, and told them the things which Jesus had done.

units.leftText: Then the chief priests and Pharisees convened the Sanhedrin and said, “What are we to do? This man is performing many signs.
units.rightText: The chief priests therefore and the Pharisees gathered a council, and said, What do we? for this man doeth many signs.
leftNotes: 11:47 Or the Council

units.leftText: If we let Him go on like this, everyone will believe in Him, and then the Romans will come and take away both our place and our nation.”
units.rightText: If we let him thus alone, all men will believe on him: and the Romans will come and take away both our place and our nation.

units.leftText: But one of them, named Caiaphas, who was high priest that year, said to them, “You know nothing at all!
units.rightText: But a certain one of them, Caiaphas, being high priest that year, said unto them, Ye know nothing at all,

units.leftText: You do not realize that it is better for you that one man die for the people than that the whole nation perish.”
units.rightText: nor do ye take account that it is expedient for you that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not.

units.leftText: Caiaphas did not say this on his own. Instead, as high priest that year, he was prophesying that Jesus would die for the nation,
units.rightText: Now this he said not of himself: but being high priest that year, he prophesied that Jesus should die for the nation;

units.leftText: and not only for the nation, but also for the scattered children of God, to gather them together into one.
units.rightText: and not for the nation only, but that he might also gather together into one the children of God that are scattered abroad.

units.leftText: So from that day on they plotted to kill Him.
units.rightText: So from that day forth they took counsel that they might put him to death.

units.leftText: As a result, Jesus no longer went about publicly among the Jews, but He withdrew to a town called Ephraim in an area near the wilderness. And He stayed there with the disciples.
units.rightText: Jesus therefore walked no more openly among the Jews, but departed thence into the country near to the wilderness, into a city called Ephraim; and there he tarried with the disciples.

units.leftText: Now the Jewish Passover was near, and many people went up from the country to Jerusalem to purify themselves before the Passover.
units.rightText: Now the passover of the Jews was at hand: and many went up to Jerusalem out of the country before the passover, to purify themselves.

units.leftText: They kept looking for Jesus and asking one another as they stood in the temple courts, “What do you think? Will He come to the feast at all?”
units.rightText: They sought therefore for Jesus, and spake one with another, as they stood in the temple, What think ye? That he will not come to the feast?
leftNotes: 11:56 Literally the temple

units.leftText: But the chief priests and Pharisees had given orders that anyone who knew where He was must report it, so that they could arrest Him.
units.rightText: Now the chief priests and the Pharisees had given commandment, that, if any man knew where he was, he should show it, that they might take him.

units.leftText: Six days before the Passover, Jesus came to Bethany, the hometown of Lazarus, whom He had raised from the dead.
units.rightText: Jesus therefore six days before the passover came to Bethany, where Lazarus was, whom Jesus raised from the dead.

units.leftText: So they hosted a dinner for Jesus there. Martha served, and Lazarus was among those reclining at the table with Him.
units.rightText: So they made him a supper there: and Martha served; but Lazarus was one of them that sat at meat with him.

units.leftText: Then Mary took about a pint of expensive perfume, made of pure nard, and she anointed Jesus’ feet and wiped them with her hair. And the house was filled with the fragrance of the perfume.
units.rightText: Mary therefore took a pound of ointment of pure nard, very precious, and anointed the feet of Jesus, and wiped his feet with her hair: and the house was filled with the odor of the ointment.
leftNotes: 12:3 Greek a litra; that is, approximately 12 ounces or 340 grams

units.leftText: But one of His disciples, Judas Iscariot, who was going to betray Him, asked,
units.rightText: But Judas Iscariot, one of his disciples, that should betray him, saith,

units.leftText: “Why wasn’t this perfume sold for three hundred denarii and the money given to the poor?”
units.rightText: Why was not this ointment sold for three hundred shillings, and given to the poor?
leftNotes: 12:5 A denarius was customarily a day’s wage for a laborer; see Matthew 20:2|MAT 20:2*.

units.leftText: Judas did not say this because he cared about the poor, but because he was a thief. As keeper of the money bag, he used to take from what was put into it.
units.rightText: Now this he said, not because he cared for the poor; but because he was a thief, and having the bag took away what was put therein.

units.leftText: “Leave her alone,” Jesus replied. “She has kept this perfume in preparation for the day of My burial.
units.rightText: Jesus therefore said, Suffer her to keep it against the day of my burying.

units.leftText: The poor you will always have with you, but you will not always have Me.” The Plot to Kill Lazarus
units.rightText: For the poor ye have always with you; but me ye have not always.
leftNotes: 12:8 See Deuteronomy 15:11|DEU 15:11*.

units.leftText: Meanwhile a large crowd of Jews learned that Jesus was there. And they came not only because of Him, but also to see Lazarus, whom He had raised from the dead.
units.rightText: The common people therefore of the Jews learned that he was there: and they came, not for Jesus’ sake only, but that they might see Lazarus also, whom he had raised from the dead.

units.leftText: So the chief priests made plans to kill Lazarus as well,
units.rightText: But the chief priests took counsel that they might put Lazarus also to death;

units.leftText: for on account of him many of the Jews were deserting them and believing in Jesus. The Triumphal Entry (Zechariah 9:9–13|ZEC 9:9-13*; Matthew 21:1–11|MAT 21:1-11*; Mark 11:1–11|MRK 11:1-11*; Luke 19:28–40|LUK 19:28-40*)
units.rightText: because that by reason of him many of the Jews went away, and believed on Jesus.

units.leftText: The next day the great crowd that had come to the feast heard that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem.
units.rightText: On the morrow a great multitude that had come to the feast, when they heard that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem,

units.leftText: They took palm branches and went out to meet Him, shouting: “Hosanna!” “Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord!” “Blessed is the King of Israel!”
units.rightText: took the branches of the palm trees, and went forth to meet him, and cried out, Hosanna: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord, even the King of Israel.
leftNotes: 12:13 Hosanna is a transliteration of the Hebrew Hosia-na, meaning Save, we pray or Save now, which became a shout of praise; see Psalm 118:25|PSA 118:25*.

units.leftText: Finding a young donkey, Jesus sat on it, as it is written:
units.rightText: And Jesus, having found a young ass, sat thereon; as it is written,

units.leftText: “Do not be afraid, O Daughter of Zion. See, your King is coming, seated on the colt of a donkey.”
units.rightText: Fear not, daughter of Zion: behold, thy King cometh, sitting on an ass’s colt.
leftNotes: 12:15 Zechariah 9:9|ZEC 9:9*

units.leftText: At first His disciples did not understand these things, but after Jesus was glorified they remembered what had been done to Him, and they realized that these very things had also been written about Him.
units.rightText: These things understood not his disciples at the first: but when Jesus was glorified, then remembered they that these things were written of him, and that they had done these things unto him.

units.leftText: Meanwhile, many people who had been with Jesus when He called Lazarus from the tomb and raised him from the dead continued to testify.
units.rightText: The multitude therefore that was with him when he called Lazarus out of the tomb, and raised him from the dead, bare witness.

units.leftText: That is also why the crowd went out to meet Him, because they heard that He had performed this sign.
units.rightText: For this cause also the multitude went and met him, for that they heard that he had done this sign.

units.leftText: Then the Pharisees said to one another, “You can see that this is doing you no good. Look how the whole world has gone after Him!” Jesus Predicts His Death
units.rightText: The Pharisees therefore said among themselves, Behold how ye prevail nothing; lo, the world is gone after him.

units.leftText: Now there were some Greeks among those who went up to worship at the feast.
units.rightText: Now there were certain Greeks among those that went up to worship at the feast:

units.leftText: They came to Philip, who was from Bethsaida in Galilee, and requested of him, “Sir, we want to see Jesus.”
units.rightText: these therefore came to Philip, who was of Bethsaida of Galilee, and asked him, saying, Sir, we would see Jesus.

units.leftText: Philip relayed this appeal to Andrew, and both of them went and told Jesus.
units.rightText: Philip cometh and telleth Andrew: Andrew cometh, and Philip, and they tell Jesus.

units.leftText: But Jesus replied, “The hour has come for the Son of Man to be glorified.
units.rightText: And Jesus answereth them, saying, The hour is come, that the Son of man should be glorified.

units.leftText: Truly, truly, I tell you, unless a kernel of wheat falls to the ground and dies, it remains only a seed. But if it dies, it bears much fruit.
units.rightText: Verily, verily, I say unto you, Except a grain of wheat fall into the earth and die, it abideth by itself alone; but if it die, it beareth much fruit.

units.leftText: Whoever loves his life will lose it, but whoever hates his life in this world will keep it for eternal life.
units.rightText: He that loveth his life loseth it; and he that hateth his life in this world shall keep it unto life eternal.

units.leftText: If anyone serves Me, he must follow Me; and where I am, My servant will be as well. If anyone serves Me, the Father will honor him.
units.rightText: If any man serve me, let him follow me; and where I am, there shall also my servant be: if any man serve me, him will the Father honor.

units.leftText: Now My soul is troubled, and what shall I say? ‘Father, save Me from this hour’? No, it is for this purpose that I have come to this hour.
units.rightText: Now is my soul troubled; and what shall I say? Father, save me from this hour. But for this cause came I unto this hour.

units.leftText: Father, glorify Your name!” Then a voice came from heaven: “I have glorified it, and I will glorify it again.”
units.rightText: Father, glorify thy name. There came therefore a voice out of heaven, saying, I have both glorified it, and will glorify it again.

units.leftText: The crowd standing there heard it and said that it had thundered. Others said that an angel had spoken to Him.
units.rightText: The multitude therefore, that stood by, and heard it, said that it had thundered: others said, An angel hath spoken to him.

units.leftText: In response, Jesus said, “This voice was not for My benefit, but yours.
units.rightText: Jesus answered and said, This voice hath not come for my sake, but for your sakes.

units.leftText: Now judgment is upon this world; now the prince of this world will be cast out.
units.rightText: Now is the judgment of this world: now shall the prince of this world be cast out.

units.leftText: And I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw everyone to Myself.”
units.rightText: And I, if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all men unto myself.

units.leftText: He said this to indicate the kind of death He was going to die.
units.rightText: But this he said, signifying by what manner of death he should die.

units.leftText: The crowd replied, “We have heard from the Law that the Christ will remain forever. So how can You say that the Son of Man must be lifted up? Who is this Son of Man?”
units.rightText: The multitude therefore answered him, We have heard out of the law that the Christ abideth for ever: and how sayest thou, The Son of man must be lifted up? who is this Son of man?

units.leftText: Then Jesus told them, “For a little while longer, the Light will be among you. Walk while you have the Light, so that darkness will not overtake you. The one who walks in the darkness does not know where he is going.
units.rightText: Jesus therefore said unto them, Yet a little while is the light among you. Walk while ye have the light, that darkness overtake you not: and he that walketh in the darkness knoweth not whither he goeth.

units.leftText: While you have the Light, believe in the Light, so that you may become sons of light.” After Jesus had spoken these things, He went away and was hidden from them. Belief and Unbelief
units.rightText: While ye have the light, believe on the light, that ye may become sons of light. These things spake Jesus, and he departed and hid himself from them.

units.leftText: Although Jesus had performed so many signs in their presence, they still did not believe in Him.
units.rightText: But though he had done so many signs before them, yet they believed not on him:

units.leftText: This was to fulfill the word of Isaiah the prophet: “Lord, who has believed our message? And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?”
units.rightText: that the word of Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled, which he spake, Lord, who hath believed our report? And to whom hath the arm of the Lord been revealed?

units.leftText: For this reason they were unable to believe. For again, Isaiah says:
units.rightText: For this cause they could not believe, for that Isaiah said again,

units.leftText: “He has blinded their eyes and hardened their hearts, so that they cannot see with their eyes, and understand with their hearts, and turn, and I would heal them.”
units.rightText: He hath blinded their eyes, and he hardened their heart; Lest they should see with their eyes, and perceive with their heart, And should turn, And I should heal them.

units.leftText: Isaiah said these things because he saw Jesus’ glory and spoke about Him.
units.rightText: These things said Isaiah, because he saw his glory; and he spake of him.

units.leftText: Nevertheless, many of the leaders believed in Him. But because of the Pharisees they did not confess Him, for fear that they would be put out of the synagogue.
units.rightText: Nevertheless even of the rulers many believed on him; but because of the Pharisees they did not confess it, lest they should be put out of the synagogue:

units.leftText: For they loved praise from men more than praise from God.
units.rightText: for they loved the glory that is of men more than the glory that is of God.

units.leftText: Then Jesus cried out, “Whoever believes in Me does not believe in Me alone, but in the One who sent Me.
units.rightText: And Jesus cried and said, He that believeth on me, believeth not on me, but on him that sent me.

units.leftText: And whoever sees Me sees the One who sent Me.
units.rightText: And he that beholdeth me beholdeth him that sent me.

units.leftText: I have come into the world as a light, so that no one who believes in Me should remain in darkness.
units.rightText: I am come a light into the world, that whosoever believeth on me may not abide in the darkness.

units.leftText: As for anyone who hears My words and does not keep them, I do not judge him. For I have not come to judge the world, but to save the world.
units.rightText: And if any man hear my sayings, and keep them not, I judge him not: for I came not to judge the world, but to save the world.

units.leftText: There is a judge for the one who rejects Me and does not receive My words: The word that I have spoken will judge him on the last day.
units.rightText: He that rejecteth me, and receiveth not my sayings, hath one that judgeth him: the word that I spake, the same shall judge him in the last day.

units.leftText: I have not spoken on My own, but the Father who sent Me has commanded Me what to say and how to say it.
units.rightText: For I spake not from myself; but the Father that sent me, he hath given me a commandment, what I should say, and what I should speak.

units.leftText: And I know that His command leads to eternal life. So I speak exactly what the Father has told Me to say.”
units.rightText: And I know that his commandment is life eternal; the things therefore which I speak, even as the Father hath said unto me, so I speak.

units.leftText: It was now just before the Passover Feast, and Jesus knew that His hour had come to leave this world and return to the Father. Having loved His own who were in the world, He loved them to the very end.
units.rightText: Now before the feast of the passover, Jesus knowing that his hour was come that he should depart out of this world unto the Father, having loved his own that were in the world, he loved them unto the end.
leftNotes: 13:1 Or He showed them the full extent of His love.

units.leftText: The evening meal was underway, and the devil had already put into the heart of Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot, to betray Jesus.
units.rightText: And during supper, the devil having already put into the heart of Judas Iscariot, Simon’s son, to betray him,

units.leftText: Jesus knew that the Father had delivered all things into His hands, and that He had come from God and was returning to God.
units.rightText: Jesus, knowing that the Father had given all things into his hands, and that he came forth from God, and goeth unto God,

units.leftText: So He got up from the supper, laid aside His outer garments, and wrapped a towel around His waist.
units.rightText: riseth from supper, and layeth aside his garments; and he took a towel, and girded himself.

units.leftText: After that, He poured water into a basin and began to wash the disciples’ feet and dry them with the towel that was around Him.
units.rightText: Then he poureth water into the basin, and began to wash the disciples’ feet, and to wipe them with the towel wherewith he was girded.

units.leftText: He came to Simon Peter, who asked Him, “Lord, are You going to wash my feet?”
units.rightText: So he cometh to Simon Peter. He saith unto him, Lord, dost thou wash my feet?

units.leftText: Jesus replied, “You do not realize now what I am doing, but later you will understand.”
units.rightText: Jesus answered and said unto him, What I do thou knowest not now; but thou shalt understand hereafter.

units.leftText: “Never shall You wash my feet!” Peter told Him. Jesus answered, “Unless I wash you, you have no part with Me.”
units.rightText: Peter saith unto him, Thou shalt never wash my feet. Jesus answered him, If I wash thee not, thou hast no part with me.

units.leftText: “Then, Lord,” Simon Peter replied, “not only my feet, but my hands and my head as well!”
units.rightText: Simon Peter saith unto him, Lord, not my feet only, but also my hands and my head.

units.leftText: Jesus told him, “Whoever has already bathed needs only to wash his feet, and he will be completely clean. And you are clean, though not all of you.”
units.rightText: Jesus saith to him, He that is bathed needeth not save to wash his feet, but is clean every whit: and ye are clean, but not all.

units.leftText: For He knew who would betray Him. That is why He said, “Not all of you are clean.”
units.rightText: For he knew him that should betray him; therefore said he, Ye are not all clean.

units.leftText: When Jesus had washed their feet and put on His outer garments, He reclined with them again and asked, “Do you know what I have done for you?
units.rightText: So when he had washed their feet, and taken his garments, and sat down again, he said unto them, Know ye what I have done to you?

units.leftText: You call Me Teacher and Lord, and rightly so, because I am.
units.rightText: Ye call me, Teacher, and, Lord: and ye say well; for so I am.

units.leftText: So if I, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also should wash one another’s feet.
units.rightText: If I then, the Lord and the Teacher, have washed your feet, ye also ought to wash one another’s feet.

units.leftText: I have set you an example so that you should do as I have done for you.
units.rightText: For I have given you an example, that ye also should do as I have done to you.

units.leftText: Truly, truly, I tell you, no servant is greater than his master, nor is a messenger greater than the one who sent him.
units.rightText: Verily, verily, I say unto you, A servant is not greater than his lord; neither one that is sent greater than he that sent him.
leftNotes: 13:16 Cited in John 15:20|JHN 15:20*

units.leftText: If you know these things, you will be blessed if you do them. Jesus Predicts His Betrayal (Psalm 41:1–13|PSA 41:1-13*)
units.rightText: If ye know these things, blessed are ye if ye do them.

units.leftText: I am not speaking about all of you; I know whom I have chosen. But this is to fulfill the Scripture: ‘The one who shares My bread has lifted up his heel against Me.’
units.rightText: I speak not of you all: I know whom I have chosen: but that the scripture may be fulfilled, He that eateth my bread lifted up his heel against me.

units.leftText: I am telling you now before it happens, so that when it comes to pass, you will believe that I am He.
units.rightText: From henceforth I tell you before it come to pass, that, when it is come to pass, ye may believe that I am he.

units.leftText: Truly, truly, I tell you, whoever receives the one I send receives Me, and whoever receives Me receives the One who sent Me.”
units.rightText: Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that receiveth whomsoever I send receiveth me; and he that receiveth me receiveth him that sent me.

units.leftText: After Jesus had said this, He became troubled in spirit and testified, “Truly, truly, I tell you, one of you will betray Me.”
units.rightText: When Jesus had thus said, he was troubled in the spirit, and testified, and said, Verily, verily, I say unto you, that one of you shall betray me.

units.leftText: The disciples looked at one another, perplexed as to which of them He meant.
units.rightText: The disciples looked one on another, doubting of whom he spake.

units.leftText: One of His disciples, the one whom Jesus loved, was reclining at His side.
units.rightText: There was at the table reclining in Jesus’ bosom one of his disciples, whom Jesus loved.
leftNotes: 13:23 Greek was reclining in the bosom of Jesus

units.leftText: So Simon Peter motioned to him to ask Jesus which one He was talking about.
units.rightText: Simon Peter therefore beckoneth to him, and saith unto him, Tell us who it is of whom he speaketh.

units.leftText: Leaning back against Jesus, he asked, “Lord, who is it?”
units.rightText: He leaning back, as he was, on Jesus’ breast saith unto him, Lord, who is it?

units.leftText: Jesus answered, “It is the one to whom I give this morsel after I have dipped it.” Then He dipped the morsel and gave it to Judas son of Simon Iscariot.
units.rightText: Jesus therefore answereth, He it is, for whom I shall dip the sop, and give it him. So when he had dipped the sop, he taketh and giveth it to Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot.

units.leftText: And when Judas had taken the morsel, Satan entered into him.
units.rightText: And after the sop, then entered Satan into him. Jesus therefore saith unto him, What thou doest, do quickly.

units.leftText: But no one at the table knew why Jesus had said this to him.
units.rightText: Now no man at the table knew for what intent he spake this unto him.

units.leftText: Since Judas kept the money bag, some thought that Jesus was telling him to buy what was needed for the feast, or to give something to the poor.
units.rightText: For some thought, because Judas had the bag, that Jesus said unto him, Buy what things we have need of for the feast; or, that he should give something to the poor.

units.leftText: As soon as he had received the morsel, Judas went out into the night. Love One Another (Romans 12:9–13|ROM 12:9-13*; 1 John 3:11–24|1JN 3:11-24*)
units.rightText: He then having received the sop went out straightway: and it was night.

units.leftText: When Judas had gone out, Jesus said, “Now the Son of Man is glorified, and God is glorified in Him.
units.rightText: When therefore he was gone out, Jesus saith, Now is the Son of man glorified, and God is glorified in him;

units.leftText: If God is glorified in Him, God will also glorify the Son in Himself — and will glorify Him at once.
units.rightText: and God shall glorify him in himself, and straightway shall he glorify him.
leftNotes: 13:32 WH does not include If God is glorified in Him.

units.leftText: Little children, I am with you only a little while longer. You will look for Me, and as I said to the Jews, so now I say to you: ‘Where I am going, you cannot come.’
units.rightText: Little children, yet a little while I am with you. Ye shall seek me: and as I said unto the Jews, Whither I go, ye cannot come; so now I say unto you.

units.leftText: A new commandment I give you: Love one another. As I have loved you, so you also must love one another.
units.rightText: A new commandment I give unto you, that ye love one another; even as I have loved you, that ye also love one another.

units.leftText: By this everyone will know that you are My disciples, if you love one another.” Jesus Predicts Peter’s Denial (Matthew 26:31–35|MAT 26:31-35*; Mark 14:27–31|MRK 14:27-31*; Luke 22:31–38|LUK 22:31-38*)
units.rightText: By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another.

units.leftText: “Lord, where are You going?” Simon Peter asked. Jesus answered, “Where I am going, you cannot follow Me now, but you will follow later.”
units.rightText: Simon Peter saith unto him, Lord, whither goest thou? Jesus answered, Whither I go, thou canst not follow me now; but thou shalt follow afterwards.

units.leftText: “Lord,” said Peter, “why can’t I follow You now? I will lay down my life for You.”
units.rightText: Peter saith unto him, Lord, why cannot I follow thee even now? I will lay down my life for thee.

units.leftText: “Will you lay down your life for Me?” Jesus replied. “Truly, truly, I tell you, before the rooster crows, you will deny Me three times.[’’]
units.rightText: Jesus answereth, Wilt thou lay down thy life for me? Verily, verily, I say unto thee, The cock shall not crow, till thou hast denied me thrice.

units.leftText: “Do not let your hearts be troubled. You believe in God; believe in Me as well.
units.rightText: Let not your heart be troubled: believe in God, believe also in me.
leftNotes: 14:1 Or Believe in God

units.leftText: In My Father’s house are many rooms. If it were not so, would I have told you that I am going there to prepare a place for you?
units.rightText: In my Father’s house are many mansions; if it were not so, I would have told you; for I go to prepare a place for you.
leftNotes: 14:2 Or If it were not so, I would have told you. I am going there to prepare a place for you.

units.leftText: And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come back and welcome you into My presence, so that you also may be where I am.
units.rightText: And if I go and prepare a place for you, I come again, and will receive you unto myself; that where I am, there ye may be also.

units.leftText: You know the way to the place where I am going. ” The Way, the Truth, and the Life
units.rightText: And whither I go, ye know the way.
leftNotes: 14:4 BYZ and TR And where I go you know, and the way you know.

units.leftText: “Lord,” said Thomas, “we do not know where You are going, so how can we know the way?”
units.rightText: Thomas saith unto him, Lord, we know not whither thou goest; how know we the way?

units.leftText: Jesus answered, “I am the way and the truth and the life. No one comes to the Father except through Me.
units.rightText: Jesus saith unto him, I am the way, and the truth, and the life: no one cometh unto the Father, but by me.

units.leftText: If you had known Me, you would know My Father as well. From now on you do know Him and have seen Him.”
units.rightText: If ye had known me, ye would have known my Father also: from henceforth ye know him, and have seen him.

units.leftText: Philip said to Him, “Lord, show us the Father, and that will be enough for us.”
units.rightText: Philip saith unto him, Lord, show us the Father, and it sufficeth us.

units.leftText: Jesus replied, “Philip, I have been with you all this time, and still you do not know Me? Anyone who has seen Me has seen the Father. How can you say, ‘Show us the Father’?
