units.rightText: Jesus saith unto him, Have I been so long time with you, and dost thou not know me, Philip? he that hath seen me hath seen the Father; how sayest thou, Show us the Father?

units.leftText: Do you not believe that I am in the Father and the Father is in Me? The words I say to you, I do not speak on My own. Instead, it is the Father dwelling in Me, performing His works.
units.rightText: Believest thou not that I am in the Father, and the Father in me? the words that I say unto you I speak not from myself: but the Father abiding in me doeth his works.

units.leftText: Believe Me that I am in the Father and the Father is in Me — or at least believe on account of the works themselves.
units.rightText: Believe me that I am in the Father, and the Father in me: or else believe me for the very works’ sake.

units.leftText: Truly, truly, I tell you, whoever believes in Me will also do the works that I am doing. He will do even greater things than these, because I am going to the Father.
units.rightText: Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that believeth on me, the works that I do shall he do also; and greater works than these shall he do; because I go unto the Father.

units.leftText: And I will do whatever you ask in My name, so that the Father may be glorified in the Son.
units.rightText: And whatsoever ye shall ask in my name, that will I do, that the Father may be glorified in the Son.

units.leftText: If you ask Me for anything in My name, I will do it. Jesus Promises the Holy Spirit (John 16:5–16|JHN 16:5-16*)
units.rightText: If ye shall ask anything in my name, that will I do.
leftNotes: 14:14 TR does not include Me.

units.leftText: If you love Me, you will keep My commandments.
units.rightText: If ye love me, ye will keep my commandments.
leftNotes: 14:15 Or If you love Me, keep

units.leftText: And I will ask the Father, and He will give you another Advocate to be with you forever —
units.rightText: And I will pray the Father, and he shall give you another Comforter, that he may be with you for ever,
leftNotes: 14:16 Or Comforter or Helper or Counselor; Greek Paraclete; also in verse 26

units.leftText: the Spirit of truth. The world cannot receive Him, because it neither sees Him nor knows Him. But you do know Him, for He abides with you and will be in you.
units.rightText: even the Spirit of truth: whom the world cannot receive; for it beholdeth him not, neither knoweth him: ye know him; for he abideth with you, and shall be in you.
leftNotes: 14:17 WH and is in you

units.leftText: I will not leave you as orphans; I will come to you.
units.rightText: I will not leave you desolate: I come unto you.

units.leftText: In a little while the world will see Me no more, but you will see Me. Because I live, you also will live.
units.rightText: Yet a little while, and the world beholdeth me no more; but ye behold me: because I live, ye shall live also.

units.leftText: On that day you will know that I am in My Father, and you are in Me, and I am in you.
units.rightText: In that day ye shall know that I am in my Father, and ye in me, and I in you.

units.leftText: Whoever has My commandments and keeps them is the one who loves Me. The one who loves Me will be loved by My Father, and I will love him and reveal Myself to him.”
units.rightText: He that hath my commandments, and keepeth them, he it is that loveth me: and he that loveth me shall be loved of my Father, and I will love him, and will manifest myself unto him.

units.leftText: Judas (not Iscariot) asked Him, “Lord, why are You going to reveal Yourself to us and not to the world?”
units.rightText: Judas (not Iscariot) saith unto him, Lord, what is come to pass that thou wilt manifest thyself unto us, and not unto the world?

units.leftText: Jesus replied, “If anyone loves Me, he will keep My word. My Father will love him, and We will come to him and make Our home with him.
units.rightText: Jesus answered and said unto him, If a man love me, he will keep my word: and my Father will love him, and we will come unto him, and make our abode with him.

units.leftText: Whoever does not love Me does not keep My words. The word that you hear is not My own, but it is from the Father who sent Me.
units.rightText: He that loveth me not keepeth not my words: and the word which ye hear is not mine, but the Father’s who sent me.

units.leftText: All this I have spoken to you while I am still with you.
units.rightText: These things have I spoken unto you, while yet abiding with you.

units.leftText: But the Advocate, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in My name, will teach you all things and will remind you of everything I have told you. Peace I Leave with You
units.rightText: But the Comforter, even the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things, and bring to your remembrance all that I said unto you.

units.leftText: Peace I leave with you; My peace I give to you. I do not give to you as the world gives. Do not let your hearts be troubled; do not be afraid.
units.rightText: Peace I leave with you; my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be fearful.

units.leftText: You heard Me say, ‘I am going away, and I am coming back to you.’ If you loved Me, you would rejoice that I am going to the Father, because the Father is greater than I.
units.rightText: Ye heard how I said to you, I go away, and I come unto you. If ye loved me, ye would have rejoiced, because I go unto the Father: for the Father is greater than I.

units.leftText: And now I have told you before it happens, so that when it does happen, you will believe.
units.rightText: And now I have told you before it come to pass, that, when it is come to pass, ye may believe.

units.leftText: I will not speak with you much longer, for the prince of this world is coming, and he has no claim on Me.
units.rightText: I will no more speak much with you, for the prince of the world cometh: and he hath nothing in me;

units.leftText: But I do exactly what the Father has commanded Me, so that the world may know that I love the Father. Get up! Let us go on from here.[’’]
units.rightText: but that the world may know that I love the Father, and as the Father gave me commandment, even so I do. Arise, let us go hence.

units.leftText: “I am the true vine, and My Father is the keeper of the vineyard.
units.rightText: I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman.

units.leftText: He cuts off every branch in Me that bears no fruit, and every branch that does bear fruit, He prunes to make it even more fruitful.
units.rightText: Every branch in me that beareth not fruit, he taketh it away: and every branch that beareth fruit, he cleanseth it, that it may bear more fruit.

units.leftText: You are already clean because of the word I have spoken to you.
units.rightText: Already ye are clean because of the word which I have spoken unto you.

units.leftText: Remain in Me, and I will remain in you. Just as no branch can bear fruit by itself unless it remains in the vine, neither can you bear fruit unless you remain in Me.
units.rightText: Abide in me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, except it abide in the vine; so neither can ye, except ye abide in me.

units.leftText: I am the vine and you are the branches. The one who remains in Me, and I in him, will bear much fruit. For apart from Me you can do nothing.
units.rightText: I am the vine, ye are the branches: He that abideth in me, and I in him, the same beareth much fruit: for apart from me ye can do nothing.

units.leftText: If anyone does not remain in Me, he is like a branch that is thrown away and withers. Such branches are gathered up, thrown into the fire, and burned.
units.rightText: If a man abide not in me, he is cast forth as a branch, and is withered; and they gather them, and cast them into the fire, and they are burned.

units.leftText: If you remain in Me and My words remain in you, ask whatever you wish, and it will be done for you.
units.rightText: If ye abide in me, and my words abide in you, ask whatsoever ye will, and it shall be done unto you.

units.leftText: This is to My Father’s glory, that you bear much fruit, proving yourselves to be My disciples. No Greater Love
units.rightText: Herein is my Father glorified, that ye bear much fruit; and so shall ye be my disciples.

units.leftText: As the Father has loved Me, so have I loved you. Remain in My love.
units.rightText: Even as the Father hath loved me, I also have loved you: abide ye in my love.

units.leftText: If you keep My commandments, you will remain in My love, just as I have kept My Father’s commandments and remain in His love.
units.rightText: If ye keep my commandments, ye shall abide in my love; even as I have kept my Father’s commandments, and abide in his love.

units.leftText: I have told you these things so that My joy may be in you and your joy may be complete.
units.rightText: These things have I spoken unto you, that my joy may be in you, and that your joy may be made full.

units.leftText: This is My commandment, that you love one another as I have loved you.
units.rightText: This is my commandment, that ye love one another, even as I have loved you.

units.leftText: Greater love has no one than this, that he lay down his life for his friends.
units.rightText: Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.

units.leftText: You are My friends if you do what I command you.
units.rightText: Ye are my friends, if ye do the things which I command you.

units.leftText: No longer do I call you servants, for a servant does not understand what his master is doing. But I have called you friends, because everything I have learned from My Father I have made known to you.
units.rightText: No longer do I call you servants; for the servant knoweth not what his lord doeth: but I have called you friends; for all things that I heard from my Father I have made known unto you.

units.leftText: You did not choose Me, but I chose you. And I appointed you to go and bear fruit — fruit that will remain — so that whatever you ask the Father in My name, He will give you.
units.rightText: Ye did not choose me, but I chose you, and appointed you, that ye should go and bear fruit, and that your fruit should abide: that whatsoever ye shall ask of the Father in my name, he may give it you.

units.leftText: This is My command to you: Love one another. The Hatred of the World
units.rightText: These things I command you, that ye may love one another.

units.leftText: If the world hates you, understand that it hated Me first.
units.rightText: If the world hateth you, ye know that it hath hated me before it hated you.

units.leftText: If you were of the world, it would love you as its own. Instead, the world hates you, because you are not of the world, but I have chosen you out of the world.
units.rightText: If ye were of the world, the world would love its own: but because ye are not of the world, but I chose you out of the world, therefore the world hateth you.

units.leftText: Remember the word that I spoke to you: ‘No servant is greater than his master.’ If they persecuted Me, they will persecute you as well; if they kept My word, they will keep yours as well.
units.rightText: Remember the word that I said unto you, A servant is not greater than his lord. If they persecuted me, they will also persecute you; if they kept my word, they will keep yours also.

units.leftText: But they will treat you like this because of My name, since they do not know the One who sent Me.
units.rightText: But all these things will they do unto you for my name’s sake, because they know not him that sent me.

units.leftText: If I had not come and spoken to them, they would not be guilty of sin. Now, however, they have no excuse for their sin.
units.rightText: If I had not come and spoken unto them, they had not had sin: but now they have no excuse for their sin.

units.leftText: Whoever hates Me hates My Father as well.
units.rightText: He that hateth me hateth my Father also.

units.leftText: If I had not done among them the works that no one else did, they would not be guilty of sin; but now they have seen and hated both Me and My Father.
units.rightText: If I had not done among them the works which none other did, they had not had sin: but now have they both seen and hated both me and my Father.

units.leftText: But this is to fulfill what is written in their Law: ‘They hated Me without reason.’
units.rightText: But this cometh to pass, that the word may be fulfilled that is written in their law, They hated me without a cause.
leftNotes: 15:25 See Psalm 35:19|PSA 35:19*, Psalm 38:19, and Psalm 69:4.

units.leftText: When the Advocate comes, whom I will send to you from the Father — the Spirit of truth who proceeds from the Father — He will testify about Me.
units.rightText: But when the Comforter is come, whom I will send unto you from the Father, even the Spirit of truth, which proceedeth from the Father, he shall bear witness of me:
leftNotes: 15:26 Or Comforter or Helper or Counselor; Greek Paraclete

units.leftText: And you also must testify, because you have been with Me from the beginning.[’’]
units.rightText: and ye also bear witness, because ye have been with me from the beginning.

units.leftText: “I have told you these things so that you will not fall away.
units.rightText: These things have I spoken unto you, that ye should not be caused to stumble.

units.leftText: They will put you out of the synagogues. In fact, a time is coming when anyone who kills you will think he is offering a service to God.
units.rightText: They shall put you out of the synagogues: yea, the hour cometh, that whosoever killeth you shall think that he offereth service unto God.

units.leftText: They will do these things because they have not known the Father or Me.
units.rightText: And these things will they do, because they have not known the Father, nor me.

units.leftText: But I have told you these things so that when their hour comes, you will remember that I told you about them. I did not tell you these things from the beginning, because I was with you. The Promise of the Holy Spirit (John 14:15–26|JHN 14:15-26*)
units.rightText: But these things have I spoken unto you, that when their hour is come, ye may remember them, how that I told you. And these things I said not unto you from the beginning, because I was with you.

units.leftText: Now, however, I am going to Him who sent Me; yet none of you asks Me, ‘Where are You going?’
units.rightText: But now I go unto him that sent me; and none of you asketh me, Whither goest thou?

units.leftText: Instead, your hearts are filled with sorrow because I have told you these things.
units.rightText: But because I have spoken these things unto you, sorrow hath filled your heart.

units.leftText: But I tell you the truth, it is for your benefit that I am going away. Unless I go away, the Advocate will not come to you; but if I go, I will send Him to you.
units.rightText: Nevertheless I tell you the truth: It is expedient for you that I go away; for if I go not away, the Comforter will not come unto you; but if I go, I will send him unto you.
leftNotes: 16:7 Or Comforter or Helper or Counselor; Greek Paraclete

units.leftText: And when He comes, He will convict the world in regard to sin and righteousness and judgment:
units.rightText: And he, when he is come, will convict the world in respect of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment:

units.leftText: in regard to sin, because they do not believe in Me;
units.rightText: of sin, because they believe not on me;

units.leftText: in regard to righteousness, because I am going to the Father and you will no longer see Me;
units.rightText: of righteousness, because I go to the Father, and ye behold me no more;

units.leftText: and in regard to judgment, because the prince of this world has been condemned.
units.rightText: of judgment, because the prince of this world hath been judged.

units.leftText: I still have much to tell you, but you cannot yet bear to hear it.
units.rightText: I have yet many things to say unto you, but ye cannot bear them now.

units.leftText: However, when the Spirit of truth comes, He will guide you into all truth. For He will not speak on His own, but He will speak what He hears, and He will declare to you what is to come.
units.rightText: Howbeit when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he shall guide you into all the truth: for he shall not speak from himself; but what things soever he shall hear, these shall he speak: and he shall declare unto you the things that are to come.

units.leftText: He will glorify Me by taking from what is Mine and disclosing it to you.
units.rightText: He shall glorify me: for he shall take of mine, and shall declare it unto you.

units.leftText: Everything that belongs to the Father is Mine. That is why I said that the Spirit will take from what is Mine and disclose it to you.
units.rightText: All things whatsoever the Father hath are mine: therefore said I, that he taketh of mine, and shall declare it unto you.

units.leftText: In a little while you will see Me no more, and then after a little while you will see Me. ” Grief Will Turn to Joy
units.rightText: A little while, and ye behold me no more; and again a little while, and ye shall see me.
leftNotes: 16:16 BYZ and TR include because I go away to the Father.

units.leftText: Then some of His disciples asked one another, “Why is He telling us, ‘In a little while you will not see Me, and then after a little while you will see Me’ and ‘Because I am going to the Father’?”
units.rightText: Some of his disciples therefore said one to another, What is this that he saith unto us, A little while, and ye behold me not; and again a little while, and ye shall see me: and, Because I go to the Father?

units.leftText: They kept asking, “Why is He saying, ‘a little while’? We do not understand what He is saying.”
units.rightText: They said therefore, What is this that he saith, A little while? We know not what he saith.

units.leftText: Aware that they wanted to question Him, Jesus said to them, “Are you asking one another why I said, ‘In a little while you will not see Me, and then after a little while you will see Me’?
units.rightText: Jesus perceived that they were desirous to ask him, and he said unto them, Do ye inquire among yourselves concerning this, that I said, A little while, and ye behold me not, and again a little while, and ye shall see me?

units.leftText: Truly, truly, I tell you, you will weep and wail while the world rejoices. You will grieve, but your grief will turn to joy.
units.rightText: Verily, verily, I say unto you, that ye shall weep and lament, but the world shall rejoice: ye shall be sorrowful, but your sorrow shall be turned into joy.

units.leftText: A woman has pain in childbirth because her time has come; but when she brings forth her child, she forgets her anguish because of her joy that a child has been born into the world.
units.rightText: A woman when she is in travail hath sorrow, because her hour is come: but when she is delivered of the child, she remembereth no more the anguish, for the joy that a man is born into the world.

units.leftText: So also you have sorrow now, but I will see you again and your hearts will rejoice, and no one will take away your joy. Ask in My Name (Matthew 18:19–20|MAT 18:19-20*)
units.rightText: And ye therefore now have sorrow: but I will see you again, and your heart shall rejoice, and your joy no one taketh away from you.

units.leftText: In that day you will no longer ask Me anything. Truly, truly, I tell you, whatever you ask the Father in My name, He will give you.
units.rightText: And in that day ye shall ask me no question. Verily, verily, I say unto you, If ye shall ask anything of the Father, he will give it you in my name.

units.leftText: Until now you have not asked for anything in My name. Ask and you will receive, so that your joy may be complete.
units.rightText: Hitherto have ye asked nothing in my name: ask, and ye shall receive, that your joy may be made full.

units.leftText: I have spoken these things to you in figures of speech. An hour is coming when I will no longer speak to you this way, but will tell you plainly about the Father.
units.rightText: These things have I spoken unto you in dark sayings: the hour cometh, when I shall no more speak unto you in dark sayings, but shall tell you plainly of the Father.

units.leftText: In that day you will ask in My name. I am not saying that I will ask the Father on your behalf.
units.rightText: In that day ye shall ask in my name: and I say not unto you, that I will pray the Father for you;

units.leftText: For the Father Himself loves you, because you have loved Me and have believed that I came from God.
units.rightText: for the Father himself loveth you, because ye have loved me, and have believed that I came forth from the Father.
leftNotes: 16:27 WH from the Father

units.leftText: I came from the Father and entered the world. In turn, I will leave the world and go to the Father.”
units.rightText: I came out from the Father, and am come into the world: again, I leave the world, and go unto the Father.

units.leftText: His disciples said, “See, now You are speaking plainly and without figures of speech.
units.rightText: His disciples say, Lo, now speakest thou plainly, and speakest no dark saying.

units.leftText: Now we understand that You know all things and that You have no need for anyone to question You. Because of this, we believe that You came from God.”
units.rightText: Now know we that thou knowest all things, and needest not that any man should ask thee: by this we believe that thou camest forth from God.

units.leftText: “Do you finally believe?” Jesus replied.
units.rightText: Jesus answered them, Do ye now believe?

units.leftText: “Look, an hour is coming and has already come when you will be scattered, each to his own home, and you will leave Me all alone. Yet I am not alone, because the Father is with Me.
units.rightText: Behold, the hour cometh, yea, is come, that ye shall be scattered, every man to his own, and shall leave me alone: and yet I am not alone, because the Father is with me.

units.leftText: I have told you these things so that in Me you may have peace. In the world you will have tribulation. But take courage; I have overcome the world!”
units.rightText: These things have I spoken unto you, that in me ye may have peace. In the world ye have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.

units.leftText: When Jesus had spoken these things, He lifted up His eyes to heaven and said, “Father, the hour has come. Glorify Your Son, that Your Son may glorify You.
units.rightText: These things spake Jesus; and lifting up his eyes to heaven, he said, Father, the hour is come; glorify thy Son, that the Son may glorify thee:

units.leftText: For You granted Him authority over all people, so that He may give eternal life to all those You have given Him.
units.rightText: even as thou gavest him authority over all flesh, that to all whom thou hast given him, he should give eternal life.
leftNotes: 17:2 Literally all flesh

units.leftText: Now this is eternal life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom You have sent.
units.rightText: And this is life eternal, that they should know thee the only true God, and him whom thou didst send, even Jesus Christ.

units.leftText: I have glorified You on earth by accomplishing the work You gave Me to do.
units.rightText: I glorified thee on the earth, having accomplished the work which thou hast given me to do.

units.leftText: And now, Father, glorify Me in Your presence with the glory I had with You before the world existed. Prayer for the Disciples
units.rightText: And now, Father, glorify thou me with thine own self with the glory which I had with thee before the world was.

units.leftText: I have revealed Your name to those You have given Me out of the world. They were Yours; You gave them to Me, and they have kept Your word.
units.rightText: I manifested thy name unto the men whom thou gavest me out of the world: thine they were, and thou gavest them to me; and they have kept thy word.

units.leftText: Now they know that everything You have given Me comes from You.
units.rightText: Now they know that all things whatsoever thou hast given me are from thee:

units.leftText: For I have given them the words You gave Me, and they have received them. They knew with certainty that I came from You, and they believed that You sent Me.
units.rightText: for the words which thou gavest me I have given unto them; and they received them, and knew of a truth that I came forth from thee, and they believed that thou didst send me.

units.leftText: I ask on their behalf. I do not ask on behalf of the world, but on behalf of those You have given Me; for they are Yours.
units.rightText: I pray for them: I pray not for the world, but for those whom thou hast given me; for they are thine:

units.leftText: All I have is Yours, and all You have is Mine; and in them I have been glorified.
units.rightText: and all things that are mine are thine, and thine are mine: and I am glorified in them.

units.leftText: I will no longer be in the world, but they are in the world, and I am coming to You.
units.rightText: And I am no more in the world, and these are in the world, and I come to thee. Holy Father, keep them in thy name which thou hast given me, that they may be one, even as we are.

units.leftText: While I was with them, I protected and preserved them by Your name, the name You gave Me. Not one of them has been lost, except the son of destruction, so that the Scripture would be fulfilled.
units.rightText: While I was with them, I kept them in thy name which thou hast given me: and I guarded them, and not one of them perished, but the son of perdition; that the scripture might be fulfilled.

units.leftText: But now I am coming to You; and I am saying these things while I am in the world, so that they may have My joy fulfilled within them.
units.rightText: But now I come to thee; and these things I speak in the world, that they may have my joy made full in themselves.

units.leftText: I have given them Your word and the world has hated them. For they are not of the world, just as I am not of the world.
units.rightText: I have given them thy word; and the world hated them, because they are not of the world, even as I am not of the world.

units.leftText: I am not asking that You take them out of the world, but that You keep them from the evil one.
units.rightText: I pray not that thou shouldest take them from the world, but that thou shouldest keep them from the evil one.
leftNotes: 17:15 Or from evil

units.leftText: They are not of the world, just as I am not of the world.
units.rightText: They are not of the world, even as I am not of the world.

units.leftText: Sanctify them by the truth; Your word is truth.
units.rightText: Sanctify them in the truth: thy word is truth.

units.leftText: As You sent Me into the world, I have also sent them into the world.
units.rightText: As thou didst send me into the world, even so sent I them into the world.

units.leftText: For them I sanctify Myself, so that they too may be sanctified by the truth. Prayer for All Believers
units.rightText: And for their sakes I sanctify myself, that they themselves also may be sanctified in truth.

units.leftText: I am not asking on behalf of them alone, but also on behalf of those who will believe in Me through their message,
units.rightText: Neither for these only do I pray, but for them also that believe on me through their word;

units.leftText: that all of them may be one, as You, Father, are in Me, and I am in You. May they also be in Us, so that the world may believe that You sent Me.
units.rightText: that they may all be one; even as thou, Father, art in me, and I in thee, that they also may be in us: that the world may believe that thou didst send me.

units.leftText: I have given them the glory You gave Me, so that they may be one as We are one —
units.rightText: And the glory which thou hast given me I have given unto them; that they may be one, even as we are one;

units.leftText: I in them and You in Me — that they may be perfectly united, so that the world may know that You sent Me and have loved them just as You have loved Me.
units.rightText: I in them, and thou in me, that they may be perfected into one; that the world may know that thou didst send me, and lovedst them, even as thou lovedst me.

units.leftText: Father, I want those You have given Me to be with Me where I am, that they may see the glory You gave Me because You loved Me before the foundation of the world.
units.rightText: Father, I desire that they also whom thou hast given me be with me where I am, that they may behold my glory, which thou hast given me: for thou lovedst me before the foundation of the world.

units.leftText: Righteous Father, although the world has not known You, I know You, and they know that You sent Me.
units.rightText: O righteous Father, the world knew thee not, but I knew thee; and these knew that thou didst send me;

units.leftText: And I have made Your name known to them and will continue to make it known, so that the love You have for Me may be in them, and I in them.”
units.rightText: and I made known unto them thy name, and will make it known; that the love wherewith thou lovedst me may be in them, and I in them.

units.leftText: After Jesus had spoken these words, He went out with His disciples across the Kidron Valley, where they entered a garden.
units.rightText: When Jesus had spoken these words, he went forth with his disciples over the brook Kidron, where was a garden, into which he entered, himself and his disciples.

units.leftText: Now Judas His betrayer also knew the place, because Jesus had often met there with His disciples.
units.rightText: Now Judas also, who betrayed him, knew the place: for Jesus oft-times resorted thither with his disciples.
leftNotes: 18:2 HF and PT Jesus also

units.leftText: So Judas brought a band of soldiers and officers from the chief priests and Pharisees. They arrived at the garden carrying lanterns, torches, and weapons.
units.rightText: Judas then, having received the band of soldiers, and officers from the chief priests and the Pharisees, cometh thither with lanterns and torches and weapons.

units.leftText: Jesus, knowing all that was coming upon Him, stepped forward and asked them, “Whom are you seeking?”
units.rightText: Jesus therefore, knowing all the things that were coming upon him, went forth, and saith unto them, Whom seek ye?

units.leftText: “Jesus of Nazareth,” they answered. Jesus said, “I am He.”
units.rightText: They answered him, Jesus of Nazareth. Jesus saith unto them, I am he. And Judas also, who betrayed him, was standing with them.

units.leftText: When Jesus said, “I am He,” they drew back and fell to the ground.
units.rightText: When therefore he said unto them, I am he, they went backward, and fell to the ground.

units.leftText: So He asked them again, “Whom are you seeking?” “Jesus of Nazareth,” they answered.
units.rightText: Again therefore he asked them, Whom seek ye? And they said, Jesus of Nazareth.

units.leftText: “I told you that I am He,” Jesus replied. “So if you are looking for Me, let these men go.”
units.rightText: Jesus answered, I told you that I am he; if therefore ye seek me, let these go their way:

units.leftText: This was to fulfill the word He had spoken: “I have not lost one of those You have given Me.”
units.rightText: that the word might be fulfilled which he spake, Of those whom thou hast given me I lost not one.
leftNotes: 18:9 See John 6:39|JHN 6:39* and John 17:12.

units.leftText: Then Simon Peter drew his sword and struck the servant of the high priest, cutting off his right ear. The servant’s name was Malchus.
units.rightText: Simon Peter therefore having a sword drew it, and struck the high priest’s servant, and cut off his right ear. Now the servant’s name was Malchus.

units.leftText: “Put your sword back in its sheath!” Jesus said to Peter. “Shall I not drink the cup the Father has given Me?”
units.rightText: Jesus therefore said unto Peter, Put up the sword into the sheath: the cup which the Father hath given me, shall I not drink it?

units.leftText: Then the band of soldiers, with its commander and the officers of the Jews, arrested Jesus and bound Him.
units.rightText: So the band and the chief captain, and the officers of the Jews, seized Jesus and bound him,

units.leftText: They brought Him first to Annas, who was the father-in-law of Caiaphas, the high priest that year.
units.rightText: and led him to Annas first; for he was father in law to Caiaphas, who was high priest that year.

units.leftText: Caiaphas was the one who had advised the Jews that it would be better if one man died for the people. Peter’s First Denial (Matthew 26:69–70|MAT 26:69-70*; Mark 14:66–68|MRK 14:66-68*; Luke 22:54–57|LUK 22:54-57*)
units.rightText: Now Caiaphas was he that gave counsel to the Jews, that it was expedient that one man should die for the people.

units.leftText: Now Simon Peter and another disciple were following Jesus. Since that disciple was known to the high priest, he also went with Jesus into the courtyard of the high priest.
units.rightText: And Simon Peter followed Jesus, and so did another disciple. Now that disciple was known unto the high priest, and entered in with Jesus into the court of the high priest;

units.leftText: But Peter stood outside at the door. Then the disciple who was known to the high priest went out and spoke to the doorkeeper, and brought Peter in.
units.rightText: but Peter was standing at the door without. So the other disciple, who was known unto the high priest, went out and spake unto her that kept the door, and brought in Peter.

units.leftText: At this, the servant girl watching the door said to Peter, “Aren’t you also one of this man’s disciples?” “I am not,” he answered.
units.rightText: The maid therefore that kept the door saith unto Peter, Art thou also one of this man’s disciples? He saith, I am not.

units.leftText: Because it was cold, the servants and officers were standing around a charcoal fire they had made to keep warm. And Peter was also standing with them, warming himself. Jesus before the High Priest (Matthew 26:57–68|MAT 26:57-68*; Mark 14:53–65|MRK 14:53-65*; Luke 22:66–71|LUK 22:66-71*)
units.rightText: Now the servants and the officers were standing there, having made a fire of coals; for it was cold; and they were warming themselves: and Peter also was with them, standing and warming himself.

units.leftText: Meanwhile, the high priest questioned Jesus about His disciples and His teaching.
units.rightText: The high priest therefore asked Jesus of his disciples, and of his teaching.

units.leftText: “I have spoken openly to the world,” Jesus answered. “I always taught in the synagogues and at the temple, where all the Jews come together. I said nothing in secret.
units.rightText: Jesus answered him, I have spoken openly to the world; I ever taught in synagogues, and in the temple, where all the Jews come together; and in secret spake I nothing.

units.leftText: Why are you asking Me? Ask those who heard My message. Surely they know what I said.”
units.rightText: Why askest thou me? ask them that have heard me, what I spake unto them: behold, these know the things which I said.

units.leftText: When Jesus had said this, one of the officers standing nearby slapped Him in the face and said, “Is this how You answer the high priest?”
units.rightText: And when he had said this, one of the officers standing by struck Jesus with his hand, saying, Answerest thou the high priest so?

units.leftText: Jesus replied, “If I said something wrong, testify as to what was wrong. But if I spoke correctly, why did you strike Me?”
units.rightText: Jesus answered him, If I have spoken evil, bear witness of the evil: but if well, why smitest thou me?

units.leftText: Then Annas sent Him, still bound, to Caiaphas the high priest. Peter’s Second and Third Denials (Matthew 26:71–75|MAT 26:71-75*; Mark 14:69–72|MRK 14:69-72*; Luke 22:58–62|LUK 22:58-62*)
units.rightText: Annas therefore sent him bound unto Caiaphas the high priest.

units.leftText: Simon Peter was still standing and warming himself. So they asked him, “Aren’t you also one of His disciples?” He denied it and said, “I am not.”
units.rightText: Now Simon Peter was standing and warming himself. They said therefore unto him, Art thou also one of his disciples? He denied, and said, I am not.

units.leftText: One of the high priest’s servants, a relative of the man whose ear Peter had cut off, asked, “Didn’t I see you with Him in the garden?”
units.rightText: One of the servants of the high priest, being a kinsman of him whose ear Peter cut off, saith, Did not I see thee in the garden with him?

units.leftText: Peter denied it once more, and immediately a rooster crowed. Jesus before Pilate (Matthew 27:11–14|MAT 27:11-14*; Luke 23:1–5|LUK 23:1-5*)
units.rightText: Peter therefore denied again: and straightway the cock crew.

units.leftText: Then they led Jesus away from Caiaphas into the Praetorium. By now it was early morning, and the Jews did not enter the Praetorium, to avoid being defiled and unable to eat the Passover.
units.rightText: They lead Jesus therefore from Caiaphas into the Prætorium: and it was early; and they themselves entered not into the Prætorium, that they might not be defiled, but might eat the passover.

units.leftText: So Pilate went out to them and asked, “What accusation are you bringing against this man?”
units.rightText: Pilate therefore went out unto them, and saith, What accusation bring ye against this man?

units.leftText: “If He were not a criminal,” they replied, “we would not have handed Him over to you.”
units.rightText: They answered and said unto him, If this man were not an evil-doer, we should not have delivered him up unto thee.

units.leftText: “You take Him and judge Him by your own law,” Pilate told them.
units.rightText: Pilate therefore said unto them, Take him yourselves, and judge him according to your law. The Jews said unto him, It is not lawful for us to put any man to death:

units.leftText: This was to fulfill the word that Jesus had spoken to indicate the kind of death He was going to die.
units.rightText: that the word of Jesus might be fulfilled, which he spake, signifying by what manner of death he should die.

units.leftText: Pilate went back into the Praetorium, summoned Jesus, and asked Him, “Are You the King of the Jews?”
units.rightText: Pilate therefore entered again into the Prætorium, and called Jesus, and said unto him, Art thou the King of the Jews?

units.leftText: “Are you saying this on your own,” Jesus asked, “or did others tell you about Me?”
units.rightText: Jesus answered, Sayest thou this of thyself, or did others tell it thee concerning me?

units.leftText: “Am I a Jew?” Pilate replied. “Your own people and chief priests handed You over to me. What have You done?”
units.rightText: Pilate answered, Am I a Jew? Thine own nation and the chief priests delivered thee unto me: what hast thou done?

units.leftText: Jesus answered, “My kingdom is not of this world; if it were, My servants would fight to prevent My arrest by the Jews. But now My kingdom is not of this realm.”
units.rightText: Jesus answered, My kingdom is not of this world: if my kingdom were of this world, then would my servants fight, that I should not be delivered to the Jews: but now is my kingdom not from hence.

units.leftText: “Then You are a king!” Pilate said. “You say that I am a king,” Jesus answered. “For this reason I was born and have come into the world, to testify to the truth. Everyone who belongs to the truth listens to My voice.”
units.rightText: Pilate therefore said unto him, Art thou a king then? Jesus answered, Thou sayest that I am a king. To this end have I been born, and to this end am I come into the world, that I should bear witness unto the truth. Every one that is of the truth heareth my voice.

units.leftText: “What is truth?” Pilate asked.
units.rightText: Pilate saith unto him, What is truth? And when he had said this, he went out again unto the Jews, and saith unto them, I find no crime in him.

units.leftText: But it is your custom that I release to you one prisoner at the Passover. So then, do you want me to release to you the King of the Jews?”
units.rightText: But ye have a custom, that I should release unto you one at the passover: will ye therefore that I release unto you the King of the Jews?

units.leftText: “Not this man,” they shouted, “but Barabbas!” ( Now Barabbas was an insurrectionist. )
units.rightText: They cried out therefore again, saying, Not this man, but Barabbas. Now Barabbas was a robber.

units.leftText: Then Pilate took Jesus and had Him flogged.
units.rightText: Then Pilate therefore took Jesus, and scourged him.

units.leftText: The soldiers twisted together a crown of thorns, set it on His head, and dressed Him in a purple robe.
units.rightText: And the soldiers platted a crown of thorns, and put it on his head, and arrayed him in a purple garment;

units.leftText: And they went up to Him again and again, saying, “Hail, King of the Jews!” and slapping Him in the face.
units.rightText: and they came unto him, and said, Hail, King of the Jews! and they struck him with their hands.

units.leftText: Once again Pilate came out and said to the Jews, “Look, I am bringing Him out to you to let you know that I find no basis for a charge against Him.”
units.rightText: And Pilate went out again, and saith unto them, Behold, I bring him out to you, that ye may know that I find no crime in him.

units.leftText: When Jesus came out wearing the crown of thorns and the purple robe, Pilate said to them, “Here is the man!”
units.rightText: Jesus therefore came out, wearing the crown of thorns and the purple garment. And Pilate saith unto them, Behold, the man!

units.leftText: As soon as the chief priests and officers saw Him, they shouted, “Crucify Him! Crucify Him!” “You take Him and crucify Him,” Pilate replied, “for I find no basis for a charge against Him.”
units.rightText: When therefore the chief priests and the officers saw him, they cried out, saying, Crucify him, crucify him! Pilate saith unto them, Take him yourselves, and crucify him: for I find no crime in him.

units.leftText: “We have a law,” answered the Jews, “and according to that law He must die, because He declared Himself to be the Son of God.”
units.rightText: The Jews answered him, We have a law, and by that law he ought to die, because he made himself the Son of God.

units.leftText: When Pilate heard this statement, he was even more afraid,
units.rightText: When Pilate therefore heard this saying, he was the more afraid;

units.leftText: and he went back into the Praetorium. “Where are You from?” he asked. But Jesus gave no answer.
units.rightText: and he entered into the Prætorium again, and saith unto Jesus, Whence art thou? But Jesus gave him no answer.

units.leftText: So Pilate said to Him, “Do You refuse to speak to me? Do You not know that I have authority to release You and authority to crucify You?”
units.rightText: Pilate therefore saith unto him, Speakest thou not unto me? knowest thou not that I have power to release thee, and have power to crucify thee?

units.leftText: Jesus answered, “You would have no authority over Me if it were not given to you from above. Therefore the one who handed Me over to you is guilty of greater sin.”
units.rightText: Jesus answered him, Thou wouldest have no power against me, except it were given thee from above: therefore he that delivered me unto thee hath greater sin.

units.leftText: From then on, Pilate tried to release Him, but the Jews kept shouting, “If you release this man, you are no friend of Caesar. Anyone who declares himself a king is defying Caesar.”
units.rightText: Upon this Pilate sought to release him: but the Jews cried out, saying, If thou release this man, thou art not Cæsar’s friend: every one that maketh himself a king speaketh against Cæsar.

units.leftText: When Pilate heard these words, he brought Jesus out and sat on the judgment seat at a place called the Stone Pavement, which in Hebrew is Gabbatha.
units.rightText: When Pilate therefore heard these words, he brought Jesus out, and sat down on the judgment-seat at a place called The Pavement, but in Hebrew, Gabbatha.
leftNotes: 19:13 Or in Aramaic; also in verses 17 and 20

units.leftText: It was the day of Preparation for the Passover, about the sixth hour. And Pilate said to the Jews, “Here is your King!”
units.rightText: Now it was the Preparation of the passover: it was about the sixth hour. And he saith unto the Jews, Behold, your King!
leftNotes: 19:14 That is, about noon

units.leftText: At this, they shouted, “Away with Him! Away with Him! Crucify Him!” “Shall I crucify your King?” Pilate asked. “We have no king but Caesar,” replied the chief priests. The Crucifixion (Psalm 22:1–31|PSA 22:1-31*; Matthew 27:32–44|MAT 27:32-44*; Mark 15:21–32|MRK 15:21-32*; Luke 23:26–43|LUK 23:26-43*)
units.rightText: They therefore cried out, Away with him, away with him, crucify him! Pilate saith unto them, Shall I crucify your King? The chief priests answered, We have no king but Cæsar.

units.leftText: Then Pilate handed Jesus over to be crucified, and the soldiers took Him away.
units.rightText: Then therefore he delivered him unto them to be crucified.

units.leftText: Carrying His own cross, He went out to The Place of the Skull, which in Hebrew is called Golgotha.
units.rightText: They took Jesus therefore: and he went out, bearing the cross for himself, unto the place called The place of a skull, which is called in Hebrew Golgotha:

units.leftText: There they crucified Him, and with Him two others, one on each side, with Jesus in the middle.
units.rightText: where they crucified him, and with him two others, on either side one, and Jesus in the midst.

units.leftText: Pilate also had a notice posted on the cross. It read: JESUS OF NAZARETH, THE KING OF THE JEWS.
units.rightText: And Pilate wrote a title also, and put it on the cross. And there was written, JESUS OF NAZARETH, THE KING OF THE JEWS.

units.leftText: Many of the Jews read this sign, because the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city, and it was written in Hebrew, Latin, and Greek.
units.rightText: This title therefore read many of the Jews, for the place where Jesus was crucified was nigh to the city; and it was written in Hebrew, and in Latin, and in Greek.

units.leftText: So the chief priests of the Jews said to Pilate, “Do not write, ‘The King of the Jews,’ but only that He said, ‘I am the King of the Jews.’ ”
units.rightText: The chief priests of the Jews therefore said to Pilate, Write not, The King of the Jews; but, that he said, I am King of the Jews.

units.leftText: Pilate answered, “What I have written, I have written.”
units.rightText: Pilate answered, What I have written I have written.

units.leftText: When the soldiers had crucified Jesus, they divided His garments into four parts, one for each soldier, with the tunic remaining. It was seamless, woven in one piece from top to bottom.
units.rightText: The soldiers therefore, when they had crucified Jesus, took his garments and made four parts, to every soldier a part; and also the coat: now the coat was without seam, woven from the top throughout.

units.leftText: So they said to one another, “Let us not tear it. Instead, let us cast lots to see who will get it.” This was to fulfill the Scripture: “They divided My garments among them, and cast lots for My clothing.” So that is what the soldiers did.
units.rightText: They said therefore one to another, Let us not rend it, but cast lots for it, whose it shall be: that the scripture might be fulfilled, which saith, They parted my garments among them, And upon my vesture did they cast lots.

units.leftText: Near the cross of Jesus stood His mother and her sister, as well as Mary the wife of Clopas and Mary Magdalene.
units.rightText: These things therefore the soldiers did. But there were standing by the cross of Jesus his mother, and his mother’s sister, Mary the wife of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene.

units.leftText: When Jesus saw His mother and the disciple whom He loved standing nearby, He said to His mother, “Woman, here is your son.”
units.rightText: When Jesus therefore saw his mother, and the disciple standing by whom he loved, he saith unto his mother, Woman, behold, thy son!

units.leftText: Then He said to the disciple, “Here is your mother.” So from that hour, this disciple took her into his home. The Death of Jesus (Psalm 22:1–31|PSA 22:1-31*; Matthew 27:45–56|MAT 27:45-56*; Mark 15:33–41|MRK 15:33-41*; Luke 23:44–49|LUK 23:44-49*)
units.rightText: Then saith he to the disciple, Behold, thy mother! And from that hour the disciple took her unto his own home.

units.leftText: After this, knowing that everything had now been accomplished, and to fulfill the Scripture, Jesus said, “I am thirsty.”
units.rightText: After this Jesus, knowing that all things are now finished, that the scripture might be accomplished, saith, I thirst.

units.leftText: A jar of sour wine was sitting there. So they soaked a sponge in the wine, put it on a stalk of hyssop, and lifted it to His mouth.
units.rightText: There was set there a vessel full of vinegar: so they put a sponge full of the vinegar upon hyssop, and brought it to his mouth.
leftNotes: 19:29 Or A jar of wine vinegar; similarly in verse 30

units.leftText: When Jesus had received the sour wine, He said, “It is finished.” And bowing His head, He yielded up His spirit. Jesus’ Side Is Pierced (Zechariah 12:10–14|ZEC 12:10-14*)
units.rightText: When Jesus therefore had received the vinegar, he said, It is finished: and he bowed his head, and gave up his spirit.

units.leftText: It was the day of Preparation, and the next day was a High Sabbath. In order that the bodies would not remain on the cross during the Sabbath, the Jews asked Pilate to have the legs broken and the bodies removed.
units.rightText: The Jews therefore, because it was the Preparation, that the bodies should not remain on the cross upon the sabbath (for the day of that sabbath was a high day), asked of Pilate that their legs might be broken, and that they might be taken away.

units.leftText: So the soldiers came and broke the legs of the first man who had been crucified with Jesus, and those of the other.
units.rightText: The soldiers therefore came, and brake the legs of the first, and of the other that was crucified with him:

units.leftText: But when they came to Jesus and saw that He was already dead, they did not break His legs.
units.rightText: but when they came to Jesus, and saw that he was dead already, they brake not his legs:

units.leftText: Instead, one of the soldiers pierced His side with a spear, and immediately blood and water flowed out.
units.rightText: howbeit one of the soldiers with a spear pierced his side, and straightway there came out blood and water.

units.leftText: The one who saw it has testified to this, and his testimony is true. He knows that he is telling the truth, so that you also may believe.
units.rightText: And he that hath seen hath borne witness, and his witness is true: and he knoweth that he saith true, that ye also may believe.

units.leftText: Now these things happened so that the Scripture would be fulfilled: “Not one of His bones will be broken.”
units.rightText: For these things came to pass, that the scripture might be fulfilled, A bone of him shall not be broken.
leftNotes: 19:36 Psalm 34:20|PSA 34:20*; see also Exodus 12:46 and Numbers 9:12.

units.leftText: And, as another Scripture says: “They will look on the One they have pierced.” The Burial of Jesus (Isaiah 53:9–12|ISA 53:9-12*; Matthew 27:57–61|MAT 27:57-61*; Mark 15:42–47|MRK 15:42-47*; Luke 23:50–56|LUK 23:50-56*)
units.rightText: And again another scripture saith, They shall look on him whom they pierced.
leftNotes: 19:37 Zechariah 12:10|ZEC 12:10*

units.leftText: Afterward, Joseph of Arimathea, who was a disciple of Jesus (but secretly for fear of the Jews), asked Pilate to let him remove the body of Jesus. Pilate gave him permission, so he came and removed His body.
units.rightText: And after these things Joseph of Arimathæa, being a disciple of Jesus, but secretly for fear of the Jews, asked of Pilate that he might take away the body of Jesus: and Pilate gave him leave. He came therefore, and took away his body.

units.leftText: Nicodemus, who had previously come to Jesus at night, also brought a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about seventy-five pounds.
units.rightText: And there came also Nicodemus, he who at the first came to him by night, bringing a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about a hundred pounds.
leftNotes: 19:39 Greek about a hundred litras; that is, approximately 34 kilograms

units.leftText: So they took the body of Jesus and wrapped it in linen cloths with the spices, according to the Jewish burial custom.
units.rightText: So they took the body of Jesus, and bound it in linen cloths with the spices, as the custom of the Jews is to bury.

units.leftText: Now there was a garden in the place where Jesus was crucified, and in the garden a new tomb in which no one had yet been laid.
units.rightText: Now in the place where he was crucified there was a garden; and in the garden a new tomb wherein was never man yet laid.

units.leftText: And because it was the Jewish day of Preparation and the tomb was nearby, they placed Jesus there.
units.rightText: There then because of the Jews’ Preparation (for the tomb was nigh at hand) they laid Jesus.

units.leftText: Early on the first day of the week, while it was still dark, Mary Magdalene went to the tomb and saw that the stone had been removed from the entrance.
units.rightText: Now on the first day of the week cometh Mary Magdalene early, while it was yet dark, unto the tomb, and seeth the stone taken away from the tomb.
leftNotes: 20:1 Literally Now on the first of the Sabbaths, early,

units.leftText: So she came running to Simon Peter and the other disciple, the one whom Jesus loved. “They have taken the Lord out of the tomb,” she said, “and we do not know where they have put Him!”
units.rightText: She runneth therefore, and cometh to Simon Peter, and to the other disciple whom Jesus loved, and saith unto them, They have taken away the Lord out of the tomb, and we know not where they have laid him.

units.leftText: Then Peter and the other disciple set out for the tomb.
units.rightText: Peter therefore went forth, and the other disciple, and they went toward the tomb.

units.leftText: The two were running together, but the other disciple outran Peter and reached the tomb first.
units.rightText: And they ran both together: and the other disciple outran Peter, and came first to the tomb;

units.leftText: He bent down and looked in at the linen cloths lying there, but he did not go in.
units.rightText: and stooping and looking in, he seeth the linen cloths lying; yet entered he not in.

units.leftText: Simon Peter arrived just after him. He entered the tomb and saw the linen cloths lying there.
units.rightText: Simon Peter therefore also cometh, following him, and entered into the tomb; and he beholdeth the linen cloths lying,

units.leftText: The cloth that had been around Jesus’ head was rolled up, lying separate from the linen cloths.
units.rightText: and the napkin, that was upon his head, not lying with the linen cloths, but rolled up in a place by itself.
leftNotes: 20:7 Greek soudarion

units.leftText: Then the other disciple, who had reached the tomb first, also went in. And he saw and believed.
units.rightText: Then entered in therefore the other disciple also, who came first to the tomb, and he saw, and believed.

units.leftText: For they still did not understand from the Scripture that Jesus had to rise from the dead. Jesus Appears to Mary Magdalene (Mark 16:9–11|MRK 16:9-11*)
units.rightText: For as yet they knew not the scripture, that he must rise again from the dead.

units.leftText: Then the disciples returned to their homes.
units.rightText: So the disciples went away again unto their own home.

units.leftText: But Mary stood outside the tomb weeping. And as she wept, she bent down to look into the tomb,
units.rightText: But Mary was standing without at the tomb weeping: so, as she wept, she stooped and looked into the tomb;

units.leftText: and she saw two angels in white sitting where the body of Jesus had lain, one at the head and the other at the feet.
units.rightText: and she beholdeth two angels in white sitting, one at the head, and one at the feet, where the body of Jesus had lain.

units.leftText: “Woman, why are you weeping?” they asked. “Because they have taken my Lord away,” she said, “and I do not know where they have put Him.”
units.rightText: And they say unto her, Woman, why weepest thou? She saith unto them, Because they have taken away my Lord, and I know not where they have laid him.

units.leftText: When she had said this, she turned around and saw Jesus standing there. But she did not recognize that it was Jesus.
units.rightText: When she had thus said, she turned herself back, and beholdeth Jesus standing, and knew not that it was Jesus.

units.leftText: “Woman, why are you weeping?” Jesus asked. “Whom are you seeking?” Thinking He was the gardener, she said, “Sir, if you have carried Him off, tell me where you have put Him, and I will get Him.”
units.rightText: Jesus saith unto her, Woman, why weepest thou? whom seekest thou? She, supposing him to be the gardener, saith unto him, Sir, if thou hast borne him hence, tell me where thou hast laid him, and I will take him away.

units.leftText: Jesus said to her, “Mary.” She turned and said to Him in Hebrew, “Rabboni!” ( which means “Teacher” ).
units.rightText: Jesus saith unto her, Mary. She turneth herself, and saith unto him in Hebrew, Rabboni; which is to say, Teacher.
leftNotes: 20:16 Or in Aramaic

units.leftText: “Do not cling to Me,” Jesus said, “for I have not yet ascended to the Father. But go and tell My brothers, ‘I am ascending to My Father and your Father, to My God and your God.’”
units.rightText: Jesus saith to her, Touch me not; for I am not yet ascended unto the Father: but go unto my brethren, and say to them, I ascend unto my Father and your Father, and my God and your God.

units.leftText: Mary Magdalene went and announced to the disciples, “I have seen the Lord!” And she told them what He had said to her. Jesus Appears to the Disciples (Luke 24:36–49|LUK 24:36-49*; 1 John 1:1–4|1JN 1:1-4*)
units.rightText: Mary Magdalene cometh and telleth the disciples, I have seen the Lord; and that he had said these things unto her.

units.leftText: It was the first day of the week, and that very evening, while the disciples were together with the doors locked for fear of the Jews, Jesus came and stood among them. “Peace be with you!” He said to them.
units.rightText: When therefore it was evening, on that day, the first day of the week, and when the doors were shut where the disciples were, for fear of the Jews, Jesus came and stood in the midst, and saith unto them, Peace be unto you.

units.leftText: After He had said this, He showed them His hands and His side. The disciples rejoiced when they saw the Lord.
units.rightText: And when he had said this, he showed unto them his hands and his side. The disciples therefore were glad, when they saw the Lord.

units.leftText: Again Jesus said to them, “Peace be with you. As the Father has sent Me, so also I am sending you.”
units.rightText: Jesus therefore said to them again, Peace be unto you: as the Father hath sent me, even so send I you.

units.leftText: When He had said this, He breathed on them and said, “Receive the Holy Spirit.
units.rightText: And when he had said this, he breathed on them, and saith unto them, Receive ye the Holy Spirit:

units.leftText: If you forgive anyone his sins, they are forgiven; if you withhold forgiveness from anyone, it is withheld.” Jesus Appears to Thomas
units.rightText: whose soever sins ye forgive, they are forgiven unto them; whose soever sins ye retain, they are retained.

units.leftText: Now Thomas called Didymus, one of the Twelve, was not with the disciples when Jesus came.
units.rightText: But Thomas, one of the twelve, called Didymus, was not with them when Jesus came.
leftNotes: 20:24 Didymus means the twin.

units.leftText: So the other disciples told him, “We have seen the Lord!” But he replied, “Unless I see the nail marks in His hands, and put my finger where the nails have been, and put my hand into His side, I will never believe.”
units.rightText: The other disciples therefore said unto him, We have seen the Lord. But he said unto them, Except I shall see in his hands the print of the nails, and put my finger into the print of the nails, and put my hand into his side, I will not believe.

units.leftText: Eight days later, His disciples were once again inside with the doors locked, and Thomas was with them. Jesus came and stood among them and said, “Peace be with you.”
units.rightText: And after eight days again his disciples were within, and Thomas with them. Jesus cometh, the doors being shut, and stood in the midst, and said, Peace be unto you.

units.leftText: Then Jesus said to Thomas, “Put your finger here and look at My hands. Reach out your hand and put it into My side. Stop doubting and believe.”
units.rightText: Then saith he to Thomas, Reach hither thy finger, and see my hands; and reach hither thy hand, and put it into my side: and be not faithless, but believing.

units.leftText: Thomas replied, “My Lord and my God!”
units.rightText: Thomas answered and said unto him, My Lord and my God.

units.leftText: Jesus said to him, “Because you have seen Me, you have believed; blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed.” The Purpose of John’s Book
units.rightText: Jesus saith unto him, Because thou hast seen me, thou hast believed: blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed.

units.leftText: Jesus performed many other signs in the presence of His disciples, which are not written in this book.
units.rightText: Many other signs therefore did Jesus in the presence of the disciples, which are not written in this book:

units.leftText: But these are written so that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that by believing you may have life in His name.
units.rightText: but these are written, that ye may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God; and that believing ye may have life in his name.
leftNotes: 20:31 Or may continue to believe

units.leftText: Later, by the Sea of Tiberias, Jesus again revealed Himself to the disciples. He made Himself known in this way:
units.rightText: After these things Jesus manifested himself again to the disciples at the sea of Tiberias; and he manifested himself on this wise.
leftNotes: 21:1 That is, the Sea of Galilee

units.leftText: Simon Peter, Thomas called Didymus, Nathanael from Cana in Galilee, the sons of Zebedee, and two other disciples were together.
units.rightText: There were together Simon Peter, and Thomas called Didymus, and Nathanael of Cana in Galilee, and the sons of Zebedee, and two other of his disciples.
leftNotes: 21:2 Didymus means the twin.

units.leftText: Simon Peter told them, “I am going fishing.” “We will go with you,” they said. So they went out and got into the boat, but caught nothing that night.
units.rightText: Simon Peter saith unto them, I go a fishing. They say unto him, We also come with thee. They went forth, and entered into the boat; and that night they took nothing.

units.leftText: Early in the morning, Jesus stood on the shore, but the disciples did not recognize that it was Jesus.
units.rightText: But when day was now breaking, Jesus stood on the beach: yet the disciples knew not that it was Jesus.

units.leftText: So He called out to them, “Children, do you have any fish?” “No,” they answered.
units.rightText: Jesus therefore saith unto them, Children, have ye aught to eat? They answered him, No.

units.leftText: He told them, “Cast the net on the right side of the boat, and you will find some.” So they cast it there, and they were unable to haul it in because of the great number of fish.
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Cast the net on the right side of the boat, and ye shall find. They cast therefore, and now they were not able to draw it for the multitude of fishes.

units.leftText: Then the disciple whom Jesus loved said to Peter, “It is the Lord!” As soon as Simon Peter heard that it was the Lord, he put on his outer garment (for he had removed it . . . ) and jumped into the sea.
units.rightText: That disciple therefore whom Jesus loved saith unto Peter, It is the Lord. So when Simon Peter heard that it was the Lord, he girt his coat about him (for he was naked), and cast himself into the sea.

units.leftText: The other disciples came ashore in the boat. They dragged in the net full of fish, for they were not far from land, only about a hundred yards.
units.rightText: But the other disciples came in the little boat (for they were not far from the land, but about two hundred cubits off), dragging the net full of fishes.
leftNotes: 21:8 Greek about two hundred cubits away; that is, approximately 300 feet or 91 meters

units.leftText: When they landed, they saw a charcoal fire there with fish on it, and some bread.
units.rightText: So when they got out upon the land, they see a fire of coals there, and fish laid thereon, and bread.

units.leftText: Jesus told them, “Bring some of the fish you have just caught.”
units.rightText: Jesus saith unto them, Bring of the fish which ye have now taken.

units.leftText: So Simon Peter went aboard and dragged the net ashore. It was full of large fish, 153, but even with so many, the net was not torn.
units.rightText: Simon Peter therefore went up, and drew the net to land, full of great fishes, a hundred and fifty and three: and for all there were so many, the net was not rent.

units.leftText: “Come, have breakfast,” Jesus said to them. None of the disciples dared to ask Him, “Who are You?” They knew it was the Lord.
units.rightText: Jesus saith unto them, Come and break your fast. And none of the disciples durst inquire of him, Who art thou? knowing that it was the Lord.

units.leftText: Jesus came and took the bread and gave it to them, and He did the same with the fish.
units.rightText: Jesus cometh, and taketh the bread, and giveth them, and the fish likewise.

units.leftText: This was now the third time that Jesus appeared to the disciples after He was raised from the dead. Jesus and Peter
units.rightText: This is now the third time that Jesus was manifested to the disciples, after that he was risen from the dead.

units.leftText: When they had finished eating, Jesus asked Simon Peter, “Simon son of John, do you love Me more than these?” “Yes, Lord,” he answered, “You know I love You.” Jesus replied, “Feed My lambs.”
units.rightText: So when they had broken their fast, Jesus saith to Simon Peter, Simon, son of John, lovest thou me more than these? He saith unto him, Yea, Lord; thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Feed my lambs.

units.leftText: Jesus asked a second time, “Simon son of John, do you love Me?” “Yes, Lord,” he answered, “You know I love You.” Jesus told him, “Shepherd My sheep.”
units.rightText: He saith to him again a second time, Simon, son of John, lovest thou me? He saith unto him, Yea, Lord; thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Tend my sheep.

units.leftText: Jesus asked a third time, “Simon son of John, do you love Me?” Peter was deeply hurt that Jesus had asked him a third time, “Do you love Me?” “Lord, You know all things,” he replied. “You know I love You.” Jesus said to him, “Feed My sheep.
units.rightText: He saith unto him the third time, Simon, son of John, lovest thou me? Peter was grieved because he said unto him the third time, Lovest thou me? And he said unto him, Lord, thou knowest all things; thou knowest that I love thee. Jesus saith unto him, Feed my sheep.

units.leftText: Truly, truly, I tell you, when you were young, you dressed yourself and walked where you wanted; but when you are old, you will stretch out your hands, and someone else will dress you and lead you where you do not want to go.”
units.rightText: Verily, verily, I say unto thee, When thou wast young, thou girdedst thyself, and walkedst whither thou wouldest: but when thou shalt be old, thou shalt stretch forth thy hands, and another shall gird thee, and carry thee whither thou wouldest not.
leftNotes: 21:18 Or others

units.leftText: Jesus said this to indicate the kind of death by which Peter would glorify God. And after He had said this, He told him, “Follow Me.” Jesus and the Beloved Disciple
units.rightText: Now this he spake, signifying by what manner of death he should glorify God. And when he had spoken this, he saith unto him, Follow me.

units.leftText: Peter turned and saw the disciple whom Jesus loved following them. He was the one who had leaned back against Jesus at the supper to ask, “Lord, who is going to betray You?”
units.rightText: Peter, turning about, seeth the disciple whom Jesus loved following; who also leaned back on his breast at the supper, and said, Lord, who is he that betrayeth thee?
leftNotes: 21:20 Greek reclined on His bosom

units.leftText: When Peter saw him, he asked, “Lord, what about him?”
units.rightText: Peter therefore seeing him saith to Jesus, Lord, and what shall this man do?

units.leftText: Jesus answered, “If I want him to remain until I return, what is that to you? You follow Me!”
units.rightText: Jesus saith unto him, If I will that he tarry till I come, what is that to thee? follow thou me.

units.leftText: Because of this, the rumor spread among the brothers that this disciple would not die. However, Jesus did not say that he would not die, but only, “If I want him to remain until I return, what is that to you?”
units.rightText: This saying therefore went forth among the brethren, that that disciple should not die: yet Jesus said not unto him, that he should not die; but, If I will that he tarry till I come, what is that to thee?

units.leftText: This is the disciple who testifies to these things and who has written them down. And we know that his testimony is true.
units.rightText: This is the disciple that beareth witness of these things, and wrote these things: and we know that his witness is true.

units.leftText: There are many more things that Jesus did. If all of them were written down, I suppose that not even the world itself would have space for the books that would be written.
units.rightText: And there are also many other things which Jesus did, the which if they should be written every one, I suppose that even the world itself would not contain the books that should be written.
